sense.def: [hoc accentu constanter in M, pro quo ubique ἐρῆμοςdesolate, solitary scribendum. Nam sic (pariterque ἑτοῖμοςready, prepared et ὁμοῖοςsimilar, like ) veteres Atticos pronuntiasse Herodiani aliorumquegrammaticorum testimoniis constat. Herodianus περὶ μον. λέξon monosyllabic words . p. 33, 1 ἐρῆμος: οὐ- δὲν εἰς μος λῆγον ὑπὲρ δύο συλλαβάς προπερισπώ- μενον τῷ η παραλήγεται, ἀλλὰ μόνον τὸ ἐρῆμοςἐρῆμος [desolate]: no word ending in -μος of more than two syllables with circumflex on the penult has η in the penult, except ἐρῆμος [desolate] . (Hom. Il. 10,520) “ὡς ἴδε χῶρον ἐρῆμον”. Ἀττικοὶ μέντοι προπαροξύνουσι τὴν λέξινas he saw the desolate place. The Attic writers, however, accent the word on the antepenult , ubi post μέντοιhowever excidisse οἱ νεώτεροιthe later writers proximum Herodiani de ἑτοῖμοςready, prepared praeceptum docet, καὶ τοῦτο δὲ παρ᾽ Αττικοῖς τοῖς νεωτέροις φασὶ προπαροξύνεσθαιand this too, they say, is accented on the antepenult by the later Attic writers . Et sic Eustath. p. 531, 40 Ἥρωδιανός φησιν ὅτι τὸ παρ᾿ Ὁμήρῳ ἐρῆμον καὶ ἑτοῖμον οἱ νεώτεροι Αττικοὶ ἀναλόγως φασὶν ἔρημον καὶ ἕτοιμονHerodian says that the Homeric ἐρῆμον [desolate] and ἑτοῖμον [ready] are said by the later Attic writers, by analogy, as ἔρημον [desolate] and ἕτοιμον [ready] . Ex quibus corrigenda quae parum accurate excerpsit Arca- dius p. 61, 6.] desertus.

[with this accent constantly in M, for which everywhere ἐρῆμος should be written. For that the ancient Attics pronounced it thus (and likewise ἑτοῖμος and ὁμοῖος) is established by the testimonies of Herodian and other grammarians. Herodian, On Monosyllabic Words, p. 33, 1: ἐρῆμος: no word ending in -μος of more than two syllables with the circumflex on the penult has η in the penult, but only ἐρῆμος. (Homer, Il. 10, 520) "when he saw the deserted place." The Attics, however, accent the word on the antepenult, where after μέντοι the words οἱ νεώτεροι seem to have fallen out, as the next precept of Herodian about ἑτοῖμος teaches: "and this too among the later Attics they say is accented on the antepenult." And so Eustathius, p. 531, 40: "Herodian says that the word ἐρῆμον and ἑτοῖμον in Homer the later Attics say analogously as ἔρημον and ἕτοιμον." From which the excerpts of Arcadius, p. 61, 6, which are somewhat inaccurate, are to be corrected.] deserted

uninvited, creeping as a feaster all day long
ἐγὼ μὲν ἕρπω πρὸς πολυστεφῆ μυχόν.
I go to the many-garlanded recess
εὐθεῖαν ἕρπε τήνδε.
go straight along this
φθονερὸν δ᾽ ὑπ᾽ ἄλγος ἕρπει προδίκοις Ἀτρείδαις
and envious pain creeps upon the Atreidae, who are first in judgment
cit.note: quod per tmesin dictum pro ὑφέρπειcreeps under .
which is said by tmesis for ὑφέρπει [creeps under].

cit.quote: ἕρπουσι
they creep
cit.note: corruptum ex πρέπουσιthey are fitting . V. πρέπωto be fitting .
corrupt from πρέπουσι [they are fitting]. See πρέπω [to be fitting].

cit.quote: ἀκτὰς ἀμφὶ Κυχρείας ἔρρουσι
They wander along the shores of Cychreia.
cit.note: ubi ἔρρουσιthey wander addidi, quod latet in litteris εραI was wandering in Mpost ἄπαιδεςchildless v. 580illatis, ex quo in apographis ἔρανταιthey have wandered factum vel ἔρρανταιthey have been scattered , quod in versum 571 transtulit Hermannus, in ἔρροντεςwandering mutatum a Blomfieldo.

where I added ἔρρουσι [they perish], which is hidden in the letters ερα in M after ἄπαιδες [childless] v. 580, from which in the copies ἔρανται or ἔρρανται was made, which Hermann transferred to verse 571, changed to ἔρροντες [perishing] by Blomfield.

cit.quote: Βακτρίων δ᾽ ἔρρει πανώλης δῆμος.
The whole people of the Bactrians perishes utterly.
ὀλοοὺς ἀπέλειπον Τυρίας ἐκ ναὸς ἔρροντας.
I left them wandering from the Tyrian ship, doomed.
ὀμμάτων δ᾽ ἐν ἀχηνίαις ἔρρει πᾶσ᾽ Ἀφροδίτα.
In the absence of eyes, all Aphrodite is gone.
ὥστε μὴ οὐ παρημελε- μένον ἔρρειν.
So as not to be neglected and perish.
ἡμῖν γὰρ ἔρρειν ἢ πρόσω τιμὰς νέμειν.
For us it is better to perish than to bestow honors further.
ἄτιμος ἔρρειν τοῦδ᾽ ἀπόξενος πέδου.
To perish dishonored, exiled from this land.
πασσάλευ᾿ ἐρρωμένως.
Nail it up vigorously.
ἐρρωμένως νῦν θεῖνε διατόρους πέδας.
Now strike the piercing fetters vigorously.
ἐρυθρὸν ἐκ μελέων πέλανον.
A red libation from the limbs.
ἐρυθρᾶς ἱερὸν χεῦμα θαλάσσης.
The sacred stream of the red sea.
ὅδε Καδμείων ἤρυξε πόλιν μάνατραπῆναι.
This man restrained the city of the Cadmeans from raging.
ἔρυμά τε χώ- ρας καὶ πόλεως σωτήριον.
A defense of the land and a savior of the city.
πρὸς ἔρυμα τόδε
To this defense
cit.note: Suspectum est, quod tumulum interpretabatur Stanleius, ut in M glossema est τὸν τάφονthe tomb . pov. Id vero ἕρμαa support, reef dicendum fuisse monuit Hermannus, ut Soph. Ant. 848 dixit πρὸς ἕρμα τυμβόχωστον ἔρ- χομαι τάφου ποταίνιονI come to the freshly heaped mound of the tomb .

It is suspect, because Stanley interpreted it as a mound, as in M the gloss is τὸν τάφον [the tomb]. But Hermann pointed out that it should be ἕρμα [a support, reef], as Sophocles Ant. 848 said πρὸς ἕρμα τυμβόχωστον ἔρχομαι τάφου ποταίνιον [I come to the freshly heaped mound of the tomb].

sense.def: Huius verbi temporibus Aeschylus praeter praesens utitur perfecto ἐλήλυθαI have come , aoristo ἦλθονI came (cum duali ἠλθέτηνthey two came Ag. 1207, ut Elmsleius recte scripsit pro ἤλθετονthey two came ) et modis reliquis ἐλθέ ἔλθοιμι ἔλθω ἐλθεῖν ἐλθώνcome, may I come, I may come, to come, having come , futuro ἐλεύσομαιI will come (pro quo Attici εἶμιI will go potius dicere solent) duobus tantum locis, Pr. 854. Suppl. 522, ut Sophocles OC. 1206. Tr. 595. venio, accedo, eo. Dicitur vel de hominibus qui aliquo veniunt vel de rebus quae alicui obtingunt.

Of this verb, Aeschylus uses, besides the present, the perfect ἐλήλυθα, the aorist ἦλθον (with dual ἠλθέτην Ag. 1207, as Elmsley correctly wrote for ἤλθετον) and the remaining moods ἐλθέ, ἔλθοιμι, ἔλθω, ἐλθεῖν, ἐλθών, the future ἐλεύσομαι (for which the Attics prefer to say εἶμι) in only two places, Pr. 854, Suppl. 522, as Sophocles OC. 1206, Tr. 595. I come, I approach, I go. It is said either of people who come somewhere or of things that befall someone.
In the proper meaning of coming, without a case.

cit.quote: λαβρόσυτος ήλθον.
I came with violent speed.
πάντως τι καινὸν ἀγγελῶν ἐλήλυθε.
He has come to announce something new.
ἀκροβόλων δ᾽ ἐπάλ- ξεων λιθὰς ἔρχεται.
A shower of stones comes from the battlements.
ἐλθὼν δ᾽ ἔοικεν οὐ και πηλεύσειν μάχην.
Having come, he seems likely to fight.
δαίμων – ἴσως ἂν ἔλθοι θαλερωτέρῳ πνεύματι.
A god—perhaps he would come with a more favorable wind.
ἐκεῖθι κῆλθον
There I came
cit.note: ab διορθωτῇto a corrector indocte illatum pro ἐκεῖθι κεῖσθονthere they two lie .
ignorantly introduced by a corrector for ἐκεῖθι κεῖσθον [to lie there].

cit.quote: ἦλθε δ᾽ αἰακτὰ πήματ᾽ οὐ λόγῳ.
Lamentable woes came, not in word.
ἐπεὶ κάτωθεν ἦλθον.
When I came from below.
μέγας τις ἦλθε δαίμων, ὥστε μὴ φρονεῖν καλῶς.
A great god came, so as not to think well.
ταχέῖά γ᾽ ἦλθε χρησμῶν πρᾶξις.
Swift indeed came the fulfillment of the oracles.
τερπνὸν τόδ᾽ ἐλθὸν φῶς ἐφήλω- σεν φρένας.
This delightful light, having come, deceived my mind.
ὅτ᾽ ἦλθ᾽ ὁ πρῶτος νύχιος ἄγγε- λος πυρός.
When the first nightly messenger of fire came.
ἐλθεῖν δ᾽ Ὀρέστην δεῦρο σὺν τύχῃ τινὶ κατεύχομαί σοι.
I pray to you that Orestes may come here with some fortune.
ἄλλος δ᾽ ὁμοίως ἦλθεν ἂν τάδ᾽ ἀγγελῶν.
Another would have come likewise to announce these things.
ὡς σαφέστερον ἀνὴρ ἀπ᾿ ἀνδρὸς τὴν νεάγγελτον φάτιν ἐλθὼν πύθηται τήνδε.
So that a man may learn more clearly from man the newly announced report, having come.
ἀλλ᾿ αὐτὸν ἐλθεῖν ἄνωχθι.
But bid him to come.
νῦν δ᾽ αὐ τρίτος ἦλθέ ποθεν σωτήρ.
Now again a third savior came from somewhere.
ὑπέρ τε πόντον ἦλθον διώκουσα.
I came over the sea in pursuit.
Ἀθη- ναία – ἔλθοι.
Athena—may she come.
ἔνθεν διώκουσ᾽ ἦλθον ἄτρυτον πόδα.
From there I came pursuing with untiring foot.
καὶ μαρτυρήσων ἦλθον.
I came to bear witness.
ὅτ᾽ ἦλ- θον Θησέως κατὰ φθόνον στρατηλατοῦσαι.
When they came, waging war against Theseus out of envy.
μήτοι τιν᾿ ἄνδρα δεῦρο πρυμνήτην χθονὸς ἐλθόντ᾽ ἐποίσειν εὖ κεκασμένον δόρυ.
Lest any man, coming here as a leader of the land, bring a well-wrought spear.
ἐγὼ δὲ ταῦτα πορσυνῶν ἐλεύσομαι.
I will come to accomplish these things.
ἐλθέτω μόρος πρὸ κοίτας γαμηλίου τυχών.
Let death come, having met me before the marriage bed.
λέγοις ἂν ἐλθὼν παισὶν Αἰγύπτου τάδε.
You may go and tell this to the sons of Aegyptus.
μηδ᾽ ὑπ᾿ ἀνάγκας γάμος ἔλθοι Κυθερείας.
May the marriage of Cytherea not come under compulsion.
Ἀντικλείας ἀσσον ἦλθε Σίσυφος.
Sisyphus came near to Anticlea.
ῥύτορες ἔλθετε
Come, deliverers.
cit.note: ubi ἔλθετεcome (plural) ego addidi.
where I added ἔλθετε [come].

sense.def: Cum dativo personae cui aliquid accidit.
With the dative of the person to whom something happens.

cit.quote: ἦλθεν αὐτῷ Ζηνὸς ἄγρυπνον βέλος.
The sleepless bolt of Zeus came upon him.
ἐναρ- γὴς βάξις ἦλθεν Ἰνάχῳ.
A clear report came to Inachus.
τίν᾿ αὐ φὴς τήνδε συμφοράν στρατῷ ἐλθεῖν;
What misfortune do you say came upon the army?
λοιμοῦ τις ἦλθε σκηπτὸς ἢ στάσις πόλει.
A plague-blast or faction came upon the city.
πῶς γὰρ λέγεις χειμῶνα ναυτικῷ στρατῷ ἐλθεῖν;
How do you say a storm came upon the naval force?
ἐμοὶ δ᾽ ἀγὼν ὅδ᾽ οὐκ ἀφρόντιστος πάλαι νείκης παλαιᾶς ἦλθε.
But this contest of ancient strife has not been unthought-of by me for a long time.
ἐλθεῖν τιν᾿ αὐτοῖς δαίμον᾽ ἢ βροτῶν τινα.
That some divinity or one of mortals came to them.
τὸ μόρσιμον μένει πάλαι, εὐχομέ- νοις δ᾽ ἂν ἔλθοι.
The fated end has long been waiting, and it may come to those who pray.
τό τοι κακὸν ποδῶκες ἔρχεται βροτοῖς.
Evil, swift-footed, comes to mortals.

sense.def: Cum accusativo viae quam quis it.
With the accusative of the way one goes.

cit.quote: κέ- λευθον ἥνπερ ήλθες.
The path by which you came.
μὴ ἔλθῃς ὁδοὺς σὺ τάσδ᾽ ἐφ᾽ ἑβδόμαις πύλαις.
Do not come on these roads to the seventh gates.

sense.def: Cum praepositionibus, et saepissime quidem cum εἰςinto .
With prepositions, and most often with εἰς.

cit.quote: τὴν σιδηρομήτορα ἐλθεῖν ἐς αἶαν.
To come to the iron-mother land.
ἐς ταυτὸν ἐλθὼν τῶν πάλαι λόγων ἴχνος.
Coming to the same track of ancient words.
Ἀργείοισι Καδμείους ἅλις ἐς χεῖ- ρας ἐλθεῖν.
For Argives to come to blows with Cadmeans is enough.
ἐλθοῦσ᾽ ἐς οἴκους.
Having come to the house.
ἐλθὼν ἐς δόμον τὸν Ἀτρειδᾶν.
Having come to the house of the Atreidae.
παραυτά δ ' ἐλθεῖν ἐς Ἰλίου πόλιν λέγοιμ᾽ ἄν.
I would say that he came immediately to the city of Ilium.
ἐς μέλαθρα καὶ δόμους ἐφεστίους ἐλθών.
Having come to the halls and hearth-homes.
ἢ καὶ τέκνων εἰς ἔργον ἠλθέτην (sic Elmsleius pro ἤλθετον) νό- μῳ;
Or did they come to the work of children by custom? (thus Elmsley for ἤλθετον)
ἐς τήνδε γαῖαν ήλθε.
He came to this land.
μηδ᾽ ἐς ἄγκρισιν ἐλθεῖν.
Not to come to a reckoning.
ἐς ἀλλόφυλον ἐλθοῦσαι χθόνα.
Having come to a foreign land.
πᾶσαν αῖαν, ἧς δί᾽ ἁγνὸς ἔρχεται Στρυμών.
The whole land through which the holy Strymon flows.
τὸν πᾶσι θεοῖς δι᾽ ἀπεχθείας ἐλθόντα
Having come into hatred with all the gods.
cit.note: de qua locutione v. Thes. vol. 3 p. 2075.
on which expression see Thes. vol. 3 p. 2075.

cit.quote: ἀνὴρ γὰρ Ἕλλην ἐξ Ἀθηναίων στρατοῦ ἐλθών.
For a Greek man came from the Athenian army.
Ἀπις γὰρ ἐλθὼν ἐκ πέρας Ναυπακτίας.
For Apis came from the shore of Naupactia.
τοιάδ᾽ ἐπ᾿ ἐχθροὺς τοὺς ἐμοὺς ἔλθοι Κύπρις.
May Cypris come upon my enemies with such things.
ἐπὶ δαιμόνων πρόδρομος ἦλθον ἀρχαῖα βρέτη.
I came as a forerunner to the ancient images of the gods.
τὰ πολλὰ βέλεα παμμιγὴ γὰς ἀπ᾿ Ἀσίδος ἦλθ᾽ ἐπ᾿ αἷαν δᾴαν.
Many mixed missiles came from the land of Asia to the hostile land.
τοιάδ᾽ ἐπ᾿ αὐτοὺς (sic ex apogr. pro αὐτοῖς) ἦλθε συμφορὰ πάθους.
Such a calamity of suffering came upon them (thus from the copy for αὐτοῖς).
βαλλὴν ἴθι ἱκοῦ, ἔλθ᾽ ἐπ᾿ ἄκρον κόρυμβον ὄχθου
Come, lord, come to the topmost peak of the hill.
cit.note: ubi correxi βαλλὴν ἔλθ᾽, ἱκοῦ τόνδ᾽ ἐπ᾿ ἄκρονcome, lord, come to this peak cet.
where I corrected βαλλὴν ἔλθ᾽, ἱκοῦ τόνδ᾽ ἐπ᾿ ἄκρον [come, reach this peak] etc.

cit.quote: ὅ τι νῦν ἦλθ᾽ ἐπὶ στόμα.
Whatever now came to my mouth.
καὶ παρ᾿ ἄκοντας ἦλθε σωφρονεῖν.
Even against their will, it came to them to be prudent.
ἅλις παρὰ Σκάμανδρον ἦλθες (recte ἦσθ᾽ margo Askewii) ἀνάρσιος.
You came to the Scamander as an enemy (rightly ἦσθ᾽ in the margin of Askew).
παρ᾿ ἄλλων χρὴ τόδ᾽ ἔρχεσθαι γέρας.
This honor must come from others.
ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἦλθες πρὸς Μολοσσὰ γάπεδα.
For when you came to the Molossian plains.
πάλιν πρὸς ῎Αργος οὐχ ἑκοῦσ᾽ ἐλεύσεται.
She will not willingly come back to Argos.
ἐρῳδιὸς γὰρ ὑψόθεν ποτώμενος ὄνθῳ σε πλήξει
For a heron flying from on high will strike you with dung.
cit.note: quod ἐρρωδιόςheron scriptum ap. schol. Hom. Od. 11, 134. Recta scri- ptura est ἐρωδιόςheron , de qua v. Thes. vol. 3 p. 2076.
which is written ἐρρωδιός [heron] in the scholium on Homer Od. 11, 134. The correct spelling is ἐρωδιός [heron], on which see Thes. vol. 3 p. 2076.

cit.quote: ἣ Διὸς θάλπει κέαρ ἔρωτι.
which warms the heart of Zeus with love.
μηδὲ κρεισσόνων θεῶν ἔρως ἄφυκτον ὄμμα προσδράκοι με
May the inescapable eye of love of the stronger gods not look upon me.
cit.note: ubi ἐμοῦ θεῶνof me, of the gods re- stitui, eiecto glossemate ἔρωςlove .
where I restored ἐμοῦ θεῶν [of me, of the gods], having ejected the gloss ἔρως [love].

cit.quote: κακοῦ δ᾽ ἔκβαλ᾽ ἔρωτος ἀρχάν.
Cast out the beginning of evil love.
ἔρως δὲ μή τις πρότερον ἐμπίπτοι στρατῷ.
May no love fall upon the army first.
ἔρως πατρώας τῆσδε γῆς σ ' ἐγύμνασεν.
Love of this fatherland has exercised you.
δηξίθυμον ἔρωτος ἄνθος.
The soul-biting flower of love.
ἔρως αἱματολοιχός.
Blood-licking love.
ὁ ἔρως
the love
cit.note: corruptum ex θέροςsummer .
corrupted from θέρος [summer].

cit.quote: παν- τόλμους ἔρωτας ἄταισι συννόμους βροτῶν.
All-daring loves, companions of the follies of mortals.
θηλυκρατής – ἔρως.
female-conquering love.
δεινὸς εὐκλείας ἔρως.
Terrible love of glory.
τῶν σ᾽ ἔρως ἔχει τυχεῖν.
Desire to obtain these things holds you.
ψεδυραὶ τρίβοι τ᾽ ἐρώτων.
Whispering paths of loves.
ἔρως δὲ γαῖαν λαμβάνει γάμου τυχεῖν.
Love seizes the earth to obtain marriage.
ἔφριξ᾽ ἔρωτι τούδε μυστικοῦ τέλους
I shuddered with love for this mystic rite.
cit.note: ubi emendavi ἔφριξ᾽ ἐρῶ δὲI shuddered, but I will say -.
where I emended to ἔφριξ᾽ ἐρῶ δὲ [I shuddered, but I will say] -.

cit.quote: ὃ δ᾽ οὖν ἐρωτᾶτε.
But what you ask.
ὑμᾶς ἐρωτῶ.
I ask you.
τὸ μήτε λέξαι μήτ᾽ ἐρωτῆσαι πάθη.
The suffering of neither speaking nor asking.
ὃς ἐρωτᾷς
You who ask
cit.note: Corrupte, ubi sensus ὅ σε θρέψαςthe one who raised you , quod Paleius con- iecit, vel simile quid postulat.
Corrupt, where the sense requires "ὅ σε θρέψας [the one who raised you]", which Paleius conjectured, or something similar.

sense.def: et composita cum ἐςinto v. 8. εἰςinto .
and compounds with ἐς, see under εἰς.

cit.quote: πολεμίων δ᾽ ἐσθή- μασι
with enemy garments
cit.note: superscripto ἐσθήματαgarments , ut est 279 πολεμίων δ᾽ ἐσθήματαenemy garments .
with superscript ἐσθήματα [garments], as at line 279 πολεμίων δ᾽ ἐσθήματα [enemy garments].

cit.quote: λακίδες ἀμφὶ σώματι στη- μορραγοῦσι ποικίλων ἐσθημάτων.
tatters around the body, dripping with threads of embroidered garments.
ἀτιμίαν γε παιδὸς ἀμφὶ σώματι ἐσθημάτων κλύουσαν.
hearing of the dishonor of her child, about the garments on her body.
ἔμπεδον σίνος ἐσθημάτων.
lasting damage to the garments.
φοι- νικοβάπτοις ἐνδυτοῖς ἐσθήμασι.
in purple-dyed garments.
ὁπόσαι στρόφον ἐσθῆ- σιν περιβάλλονται.
as many as wrap a band around their clothing.
ἐκδύων ἐμὲ χρηστη- ρίαν ἐσθῆτα.
stripping me of my prophetic clothing.
οὐ γὰρ Ἀργολὶς ἐσθὴς γυναικῶν.
For the clothing of the women is not Argive.
φαγέδαιναν, ἥ μου σάρκας ἐσθίει ποδός.
a cancer, which eats the flesh of my foot.
ἐσθλός Ἰμαῖος.
noble Imaeus.
ἐσθλά σοι πέμπειν.
to send you good things.
καὶ φέρει σαφές τι πρᾶγος ἐσθλὸν ἢ κακὸν κλύειν.
and it brings a clear matter, good or bad, to hear.
ὅ τ᾽ ἐσθλὸς Ἀριόμαρδος.
and noble Ariomardus.
Ἀρταφρένης — ἐσθλός.
Artaphrenes — noble.
πολλῶν γὰρ ἐσθλῶν τήνδ᾽ ὄνησιν εἱλόμην.
For I chose the benefit of many good things.
ἐσθλά τις δοκῶν ὁρᾶν.
someone thinking he sees good things.
δωμάτων κύνα ἐσθλὴν ἐκείνῳ.
a good dog of the house for him.
ἐσθλά
good things
cit.note: corruptum ex ἔδεθλαfoundations , quod v.
corrupt from ἔδεθλα [foundations], which see.

cit.quote: ἡμῖν δὲ πομπὸς ἴσθι τῶν ἐσθλῶν ἄνω.
Be our escort of good things upward.
ἐλευθέροις νυν ἐσθλὰ κηρυκευέτω.
Let him now proclaim good things to free men.
ἔσθει βορὰν ἄσωτον.
he eats food that cannot be saved.

sense.def: (recta haec est scriptura vocabuli ab ἕζωto sit derivandi, non quae frequens in libris est ἐσμόςswarm : de quo allatis grammaticorum testimoniis dictum est in Thes. vol. 3 p. 2092. In M. spiritus apparet nusquam: nam in tribus ubi legitur locis cum de particula coaluit in deσμόνswarm et δεσμόςbond ) turba.

(this is the correct spelling of the word derived from ἕζω, not the frequent one in the books, ἐσμός: about which, with testimonies of grammarians, it is said in Thes. vol. 3 p. 2092. In M. the breathing appears nowhere: for in the three places where it is read, it has coalesced with the particle into δεσμόν and δεσμός) crowd.

cit.quote: ἀρσενοπληθῆ δ᾽ ἑσμὸν ὑβριστὴν Αἰγυπτογενῆ.
a male-abounding, violent swarm, Egyptian-born.
ἐν ἁγνῷ δ᾽ ἑσμός
and in the holy swarm
νούσων δ᾽ ἑσμὸς ἀπ᾿ ἀστῶν ἴζοι κρατὸς ἀτερπής.
and a swarm of diseases from the citizens, unpleasant, may sit upon the head.
πρὸς ἑσπέρους τόπους.
toward the western regions.

sense.def: quum ex ἐςinto et τεand compositum sit (ut recte Etym. M. p. 382, 7), ut ὥστεso that ex ὡςas et τe, ego divisim scripsi ἔς τεinto and , ut ab verbo ἐστyou are é distinguerem, quemadmodum ὅτιthat pronomen divisim scribimus, ut ab ὅτιthat particula distinguatur. In aliorum scriptorum codicibus interdum ἕστεuntil cum spiritu aspero scribitur, secundum grammaticorum quorundam opinionem (v. Eustath. p. 162, 42), qui ex ἕως τεuntil ortum esse putabant. donec.

since it is composed of ἐς and τε (as rightly Etym. M. p. 382, 7), as ὥστε from ὡς and τε, I have written separately ἔς τε, to distinguish it from the verb ἐστέ, just as we write the pronoun ὅτι separately, to distinguish it from the particle ὅτι. In manuscripts of other writers sometimes ἕστε is written with a rough breathing, according to the opinion of certain grammarians (see Eustath. p. 162, 42), who thought it arose from ἕως τε. until.

cit.quote: ἔστε δή σφιν ἀντολὰς ἐγὼ ἄστρων ἔδειξα.
until I showed them the risings of the stars.
ἔστε δὴ πατρὶ ἔτλην γεγωνεῖν.
until I dared to speak to my father.
ἔστ᾽ ἀφίκετο.
until he came.
cit.note: Sic Stanleius pro εἰτ᾽ ἀφίκετοthen he came .
Thus Stanley for εἰτ᾽ ἀφίκετο [then he came].

cit.quote: ἔστ᾽ ἂν Διὸς φρόνημα λωφήσῃ χόλου.
until the mind of Zeus ceases from anger.
ἔστ᾽ ἂν καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ προσμάθης.
until you learn the rest too.
ἔστ᾽ ἂν ἐξίκῃ πρὸς Γοργόνεια πεδία.
until you reach the Gorgonean plains.
ἔστ᾽ ἂν πρὸς ἀνδρὸς αἵματος καθαρσίου σφαγαὶ καθαιμάξωσι.
until the slaughters of a man's purifying blood make it bloody.

sense.def: ara, focus domesticus. Dicitur de aris domesticis deorum, praesertim Vestae, quae ipsa ἙστίαHestia appellatur.
altar, domestic hearth. It is said of the domestic altars of the gods, especially of Vesta, who herself is called Ἑστία.

cit.quote: μήλοισιν αἱμάσσον- τας ἑστίας θεῶν.
staining the hearths of the gods with sheep's blood.
πρὸς ἑστία θεοῦ Φοί- βου.
to the hearth of the god Phoebus.
ήσαι φυλάσσων ἑστίας ἐμῆς πέλας.
guarding near my hearth.
cit.note: de eodem.
about the same.

cit.quote: κρατύνεις βωμὸν ἑστίαν χθονός.
you hold the altar, the hearth of the land.
τὰ μὲν γὰρ ἑστίας μεσομφάλου ἕστηκεν ἤδη μῆλα,
For the sheep of the central hearth already stand,
ἕως ἂν αἴθῃ πῦρ ἐφ᾽ ἑστίας ἐμῆς Αἴγισθος.
as long as Aegisthus keeps the fire burning on my hearth.
προστρόπαιος ἑστίας μολών.
having come as a suppliant to the hearth.
ἰὼ πάνοιζυς ἑστία.
Alas, all-wretched hearth.
τίω δ᾽ ἀθέρμαντον ἑστίαν δόμων.
I honor the unheated hearth of the house.
οὐδ᾽ ἐφ᾽ ἑστίαν (sic correxit Turnebus pro ἐφέστιον) ἄλλην τραπέσθαι.
nor to turn to another hearth (thus Turnebus corrected for ephestion).
ἐν στέγη τις ἥμενος παρ᾿ ἑστίᾳ.
someone sitting in the house by the hearth.

sense.def: Sensu latiore de laribus sive domo dicitur.
In a broader sense it is said of the household gods or the home.

cit.quote: οὐδ᾽ ἀφ᾽ ἑστίας συθείς.
nor having rushed from the hearth.
τὰ μὲν κατ᾿ οἴκους ἐφ᾽ ἑστίας ἄχη.
the griefs in the house at the hearth.
σοῦ μο- λόντος δωματῖτιν ἑστίαν.
when you came to the hearth of the house.
ὦ σωτῆρες ἑστίας πατρός.
O saviors of the paternal hearth.
ὅταν ἀφ᾿ ἑστίας μύσος πᾶν ἐλάσῃ.
when he drives all pollution from the hearth.
ἥκουσιν ἐκ- φυγόντες – ἐφ᾽ ἑστιοῦχον γαῖαν.
they have come, having fled – to the land that holds the hearth.
εἰ γάρ τιν᾿ ἑστιοῦχον ὄψομαι μόνον, μίαν παρείρας πλε- κτάνην χειμάρροον στέγην πυρώσω
For if I see any one who keeps the hearth, only one, I will set fire to the roof, letting loose a torrential flame.
cit.note: ubi nihil aliud significare potest quam ad focum s. domi versantem, si recte legitur μόνονonly , quod in ψόλονsmoke mutari volebat Musgravius, in δόμωνof the house Dobraeus Advers. vol. 2 p. 31.

where it can mean nothing other than one who stays at the hearth or at home, if μόνον [only] is correctly read, which Musgrave wanted to change to ψόλον [smoke], and Dobree in Adversaria vol. 2 p. 31 to δόμων [of the house].

cit.quote: πρὸς ἐσχάραν Φοίβου.
to the hearth of Phoebus.
ἐπ᾿ ἐσχάρᾳ πυρὸς ἔθυον.
they sacrificed on the hearth of fire.
λιπαροθρόνοισιν ἡμένας ἐπ᾽ ἐσχάραις.
seated on shining-throned hearths.
γᾶς ἔσχατον τόπον.
the furthest place of the earth.
γῆς ἐπ᾿ ἐσχάτοις ὅροις.
on the furthest borders of the land.
ἔστιν πόλις Κά- νωβος ἐσχάτη χθονός.
there is a city, Canobus, the furthest of the land.
ὀρσολοπεῖται θυμὸς ἔσωθεν.
my heart is stirred from within.
ὑμνωδεῖ θρῆνον Ἐρινύος αὐτοδίδακτος ἔσωθεν θυμός.
the self-taught heart within sings the dirge of the Fury.
τὸν ἔσωθεν (sic Seidlerus pro ἔσω) μελάθρων.
the one within (thus Seidler for ἔσω) the halls.
οἵ τ᾽ ἔσωθε δωμάτων
and those within the house
cit.note: Sed, cum Hermanno ἔσωwithin scribere malui quam in antistr. v. 812 ξυλλάβοιτοmay he take part pro ξυλλάβοιmay he take .
But, with Hermann, I preferred to write ἔσω [within] rather than in the antistrophe v. 812 ξυλλάβοιτο [may he take part] for ξυλλάβοι [may he take].

cit.quote: ἀγαθῶν ἑτάρων.
of good companions.
φρουρᾶς ἐτείας μῆχος.
the length of a year's watch.

sense.def: et contr. ἘτεοκλῆςEteocles Eteocles, qui in scenam prodit in Septem ad Thebas.
and contracted Ἐτεοκλῆς [Eteocles], who comes on stage in the Seven against Thebes.

cit.quote: Ἐτεοκλέης
Eteocles
cit.note: in initio trimetri syllaba tertia longa potius quam brevi, pariterque 39 Ἐτεόκλεες, φέριστε Καδμείων ἄναξEteocles, bravest lord of the Cadmeans , et 1007 Ἐτεοκλέα μὲν τόνδ᾽ ἐπ᾿ εὐνοίᾳ χθονὸς θάπτειν ἔδοξεit was decided to bury this Eteocles for his goodwill to the land .

at the beginning of the trimeter the third syllable is long rather than short, and likewise 39 Ἐτεόκλεες, φέριστε Καδμείων ἄναξ [Eteocles, bravest lord of the Cadmeans], and 1007 Ἐτεοκλέα μὲν τόνδ᾽ ἐπ᾿ εὐνοίᾳ χθονὸς θάπτειν ἔδοξε [it was decided to bury this Eteocles for his goodwill to the land].
διορθωτήςcorrector in margine M adscripsit Ἐτεόκλεις ἀρχηγέταEteocles, leader .
the corrector wrote in the margin of M Ἐτεόκλεις ἀρχηγέτα [Eteocles, leader].

cit.quote: τρίτῳ γὰρ Ετεόκλῳ τρίτος πάλος ἐξ ὑπτίου ᾿πή- δησεν εὐχάλκου κράνους.
For third, for Eteoclus, the third lot leapt from the upturned bronze-cheeked helmet.

form.gloss: giving victory to one side, aiding one party

sense.def: aliis opitulatus, alteri parti auxilium ferens.
aiding others, bringing help to one side.

cit.quote: ῎Αρης ἑτεραλκής
Ares, giver of victory to one side
cit.note: ubi schol. per νικηφόροςvictory-bringing exp. Est vocabulum Ho- mericum, de quo v. Thes. vol. 3 p. 2125.
where the scholiast explains it by νικηφόρος [victory-bringing]. It is a Homeric word, on which see Thesaurus vol. 3 p. 2125.

sense.def: in alteram partem vergens s. inclinans.
turning or inclining to one side.

cit.quote: Ζεὺς ἑτερορρεπής.
Zeus who inclines the balance.
ἄτην ἑτέραν ἐπάγουσαν ἐπ᾿ ἄτῃ.
bringing one ruin upon another.
ἕτερον ἐν κάρᾳ μιάστορ᾽ ἐκ κείνου πάσεται.
he will beget another avenger upon his head from that one.
θυσίαν ἑτέραν, ἄνομόν τιν᾽, άδαιτον.
another sacrifice, lawless, unfeasted.
κάμψαι διαύλου θάτερον κῶλον πάλιν.
to bend back the other leg of the double course.
δυοῖν λόγοιν σε θατέρῳ δωρήσομαι
I will present you with one of two choices.
cit.note: i.e. alterutro.
i.e. one of two.

cit.quote: δυοῖν δὲ θάτερον βουλήσεται.
he will wish for one of two things.
πόλιν δορίπονον μὴ προδῶθ᾽ ἑτεροφώνῳ στρατῷ
Do not betray the spear-toiling city to an army of different speech.
cit.note: ubi metrum aliud huius significationis vocabulum postulat, quale est ἑτεροβάγμονιwith different step , quod finxit Hermannns.
where the metre requires another word of this meaning, such as ἑτεροβάγμονι [with different step], which Hermann coined.

cit.quote: ἐγὼ δὲ πρὸς σὲ πότερον ὡς ἔτην λέγω;
But do I address you as a citizen or as a friend?
οὔτε δῆμος οὔτ᾽ ἔτης ἀνήρ.
Neither a man of the people nor a citizen.
τοῦτ᾽ ἐτήτυμον;
Is this true?
εἰ τὸ μάταν ἀπὸ φροντίδος ἄχθος χρὴ βαλεῖν ἐτητύμως.
If the vain burden of care must truly be cast away.
εἰ δ᾽ ἐτητύμως, τίς οἶδεν;
But if it is truly so, who knows?
τίς ποτ᾽ ὠνόμαζεν ὧδ᾽ ἐς τὸ πᾶν ἐτητύμως;
Who ever named her so truly in all respects?
εἰ δ᾽ ἐτητύμως μόρον τὸν αὑτῆς οἶσθα.
But if you truly know her fate.
ἔθιγε δ᾽ ἐν μάχᾳ χερὸς ἐτητύμως (sic Scaliger pro ἐτήτυμος) Διὸς κόρα.
And in battle the daughter of Zeus truly touched his hand (thus Scaliger for ἐτήτυμος [true]).
ἥξω διαιρεῖν τοῦτο πρᾶγμ᾽ ἐτητύμως.
I will come to decide this matter truly.
περίφοβόν μ᾿ ἔχει τάρβος ἐτητύμως.
Truly a fearful terror holds me.

sense.def: still, yet. With the present tense.

cit.quote: τὸν ἐλλεί- ποντ᾽ ἔτι ἥβης ἀκμαίας.
Him who is still lacking in vigorous youth.
τί οὖν ἔτ᾽ ἂν σαίνοι- μεν ὀλέθριον μόρον;
Why then should we still fawn upon a deadly fate?
νῦν δ᾽ ἔτι ζεῖ.
But now it still boils.
ἔτ᾽ ἄρ᾽ Ἀθηνῶν ἔστ᾽ ἀπόρθητος πόλις;
Is the city of Athens still unsacked?
πῶς ἂν ἐκ τούτων ἔτι πράσσοιμεν;
How could we still prosper from these things?
κοὐδέπω κακῶν κρηπὶς ὕπεστιν, ἀλλ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἐκπιδύεται.
And not yet is the foundation of evils laid, but it still gushes forth.
ἔτι γὰρ θεόθεν καταπνείει πειθώ μολπᾶν.
For still from the gods breathes persuasion of songs.
καπνῷ δ᾽ ἁλοῦσα νῦν ἔτ᾽ εὔσημος πόλις.
And the city, taken by smoke, is still conspicuous.
ἅπαξ ἔτ᾽ εἰ- πεῖν ῥῆσιν ἢ θρῆνον θέλω.
Once more I wish to speak a speech or a dirge.
ἔτι σε χρή – τύμμα τύμματι τῖσαι.
Still you must pay blow for blow.
ἔτ᾽ ἂν σέβοι δί- καν.
Still he would revere justice.
ἔτι — τέμνω
Still — I cut
cit.note: loco interpolato, quem eiecto ἔτιstill aliter scripsi.
in an interpolated passage, which I wrote differently after removing ἔτι [still].

cit.quote: παῖς ἔτ᾿ ὧν ἐν σπαργάνοις.
While still a child in swaddling clothes.
ἕως δ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἔμφρων εἰμί.
As long as I am still in my right mind.
ποταίνιον γὰρ αἷμά σοι χεροῖν ἔτι.
For fresh blood is still on your hands.
ἄλλ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἂν θείη.
But still he would set.
εὔελπίς εἰμι τὢνδέ σ᾽ ἐκ δεσμῶν ἔτι λυ- θέντα μηδὲν μεῖον ἰσχύσειν Διός.
I am hopeful that you, released from these bonds, will still be no less strong than Zeus.
ἢ μὴν ἔτι Ζεὺς, καίπερ αὐθάδη φρονῶν, ἔσται ταπεινός.
Verily Zeus, though thinking arrogant thoughts, will still be humbled.
ποῖ δ᾽ ἔτι τέλος ἐπάγει θεός;
To what end does the god still bring it?
cit.note: ubi correxl ποῖ δὲ τέλος προβὰς ἐπάξει θεόςto what end will the god bring it as it advances? ;
where I corrected to ποῖ δὲ τέλος προβὰς ἐπάξει θεός; [to what end will the god bring it as it advances?]

cit.quote: ἀλλ᾽ ἐγώ σ᾽ ἐν ὑστέραισιν ἡμέραις μέτειμ᾽ ἔτι.
But I will still pursue you in later days.
πολλῆς δὲ χώρας τῆσδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἀκροθίνια – ἔχουσ᾽ ἐσαεὶ τόνδ᾽ ἐπαινέσεις λόγον.
And of this great land still the first-fruits — you will praise this saying forever.

sense.def: ἔτιstill cum vocabulis negativis coniunctum Latino respondet amplius. Frequentissimum est οὐκ ἔτιno longer in codicibus vel sic vel coniunctim scriptum οὐκ- έτιno longer , de quo suo loco dicetur. Reliqua haec sunt.

ἔτι [still] joined with negative words corresponds to Latin amplius [any longer]. Most frequent is οὐκ ἔτι [no longer] in manuscripts written either separately or together as οὐκ- έτι, about which will be said in its proper place. The remaining instances are these.

cit.quote: κοὐδὲν ἐμποδὼν ἔτι.
And no longer any hindrance.
οὐδ᾽ ἔτι γλῶσσα βροτοῖσιν ἐν φυλακαῖς.
No longer is the tongue under guard for mortals.
μηδ ' ἔτι Νείλου προχοὰς σέβωμεν ὕμνοις.
Let us no longer worship the streams of the Nile with hymns.
ἀλλ᾽ ἄθλον ἄν σοι τοῦδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἀλγίω πόροι.
But may he grant you a prize still more painful than this.
cit.note: Sic Elmsleius pro τοῦ- δέ γ᾽ ἀλγίωmore painful than this .
Thus Elmsley for τοῦ- δέ γ᾽ ἀλγίω [more painful than this].

cit.quote: οὐ γὰρ σὺ παῖς τε κάτι τοῦδ᾽ ἀνούστερος;
For are you not a child and still more foolish than this?
θεοῦ δ᾽ ἔτ᾿ ἰσχὺς καθυπερ- τέρα.
But the strength of the god is still superior.
καὶ τίς γένοιτ᾽ ἂν τῆσδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἐχ- θίων τύχη;
And what fate could be still more hateful than this?
τίν᾿ οὐν ἔτ᾽ ἄλλον τῇδε προστιθῶ στάσει;
Whom else then shall I add to this faction?
ἐμασχαλίσθη δ᾽, ἔθ᾽ ὡς τόδ᾽ εἰδῇς.
He was mutilated, so that you may know this too.
τίν᾽ οὐν κικλήσκω τῶνδε δαιμόνων ἔτι;
Which of these divinities shall I call upon further?
τίν᾽ οὖν ἔτ᾽ ἄλλον τῆσδε βλαστημὸν λέγεις;
What other offspring of this land do you speak of?
καὶ τἄλλα πόλλ᾽ ἐπεικάσαι δίκαιον ἦν
And it was right to compare many other things.
cit.note: ubi κατ᾿ ἄλλαin other respects coniecit Wellauerus.
where Wellauer conjectured κατ᾿ ἄλλα [in other respects].

sense.def: [nam hoc accentu veteres Attici, ut ἐρῆμοςdeserted, solitary et ὁμοῖοςlike, similar , de quo disertis constat Herodiani περὶ μον. λέξon monosyllabic words . p. 33, 10 aliorumque grammaticorum testimoniis in Thesauro indicatis vol. 3 p. 2160. Hoc igitur ubique restituendum, licet in M aliorumque scriptorum codicibus prope constanter ἕτοιμοςready, prepared scriptum sit, quod Ἀττικοῖς τοῖς νεωτέροιςto the later Attic writers tribuit Herodianus 1. c. et apud Arca- dium p. 61, 22, ubi κοινὸνcommon dicitur.] paratus.

cit.quote: τοιοίδ᾽ ἕτοιμοι λαμπαδηφόρων νόμοι
such are the ready customs of the torch-bearers
cit.note: vitiose pro τοιοίδε τοί μοιsuch things to me , quod restituit Schuetzius.
corruptly for τοιοίδε τοί μοι [such things to me], which Schuetz restored.

cit.quote: τῷ δυσπραγοῦντι δ᾽ ἐπιστενάχειν πᾶς τις ἕτοιμος.
everyone is ready to lament for the unfortunate.
ζευχθεὶς ἕτοιμος ἦν ἐμοὶ σειραφόρος.
yoked, he was ready as my trace-horse.
πρὸς δὲ καρδίᾳ φόβος ἄδειν ἕτοιμος.
and at my heart fear is ready to sing.
ἑτοιμότερα γέλωτος ἀνέφερον λίβη.
they brought libations more ready than laughter.
αστει
αστει
cit.note: in litteris corruptis μήnot Hermanno latere videbatur ἑτοίμηready (feminine) , parum probabiliter.
in the corrupt letters μή [not] Hermann thought ἑτοίμη [ready] was hidden, with little probability.

cit.quote: δέκατον μὲν ἔτος τόδε.
this is the tenth year.
δεκάτῳ (δεκάτου Wunderus) σε φέγγει τῷδ᾽ ἀφικόμην ἔτους.
in the tenth (Wunder: tenth) year of this light I have come to you.
γνώσει δὲ τάδ᾽ ὡς ἔτυμα.
you will know that these things are true.
τὰν ταλαίπωρον ὡδ᾽ ἔτυμα (in apogr. nonnulla ἐτήτυμα) προσθροεῖς.
you address the wretched woman with such true (in some copies: true) words.
ἔτυμος ἄγγελος.
a true messenger.
πολλά δ᾽ ἔτυμα παιδότρωτα πάθεα προσμένει τοκεῦσιν.
many true child-wounding sufferings await the parents.
ἐτύμως δακρυχέων ἐκ φρενός.
truly weeping from the heart.
δυσσεβίας μὲν ὕβρις τέκος ὡς ἐτύμως.
as truly as insolence is the child of impiety.
ὕβριν δ᾽ ἐτύμως στυγοῦντες.
truly hating insolence.
cit.note: Sic ex apogr. pro ἑτοίμωςreadily .
Thus from the copies for ἑτοίμως [readily].

sense.def: bene, recte, ut convenit. Coniungitur cum verbis quibusvis. Inprimis frequentia sunt εὖ φρονεῖνto be well-minded (quod vel bene sapere vel bene velle signi- ficat, de quo s. v. φρονέωto think dicetur), εὖ δρᾶν τιναto do good to someone beneficio aliquem afficere, cui oppositum est ev πάσχεινto suffer beneficio affici, εὖ πράσσεινto fare well bonum quid consequi. Horum aliorumque verborum exempla secundum fabularum ordinem disposita collegit Wellauerus, quae apponimus correctis quibus Wellauerus vitiose scriptis usus erat.

well, rightly, as is fitting. It is joined with any verbs. Especially frequent are εὖ φρονεῖν [to be well-minded] (which means either to be wise or to be well-disposed, about which will be said under φρονέω), εὖ δρᾶν τινα [to do well to someone] to bestow a benefit on someone, to which is opposed εὖ πάσχειν [to be well-treated] to receive a benefit, εὖ πράσσειν [to fare well] to obtain something good. Wellauer collected examples of these and other verbs arranged according to the order of the plays, which we append, correcting those which Wellauer had used in corruptly written form.

cit.quote: κέρδιστον εὖ φρονοῦντα μὴ φρονεῖν δοκεῖν.
it is most profitable to be wise but not to seem wise.
εὖ γὰρ φρονοῦντος ὄμμα σοῦ κατηγορεῖ.
for the eye of one who is wise accuses you.
εὖ φρονῶν ἐμοί.
being well-disposed to me.
ἀλλ᾽ ἡ φρονεῖς εὖ τοῖσι νῦν ἠγγελμένοις;
but are you pleased with what has now been announced?
ὅσοι παθόντες εὖ κακοῦσί μ᾽ ἐκδίκως.
as many as, having been well treated, wrong me unjustly.
εὖ δρῶσαν, εὖ πά- σχουσαν, εὖ τιμωμένην.
doing well, suffering well, being honored well.
εἰ μὲν γὰρ εὖ πράξαιμεν, αἰτία θεοῦ.
for if we fare well, the cause is a god's.
πόλις γὰρ εὖ πράσσουσα δαίμονας τίει.
for a city that fares well honors the gods.
πόλιν μὲν εὖ πράσσουσαν.
a city faring well.
πράξας μὲν εὖ.
having fared well.
εὖ πράσσοντας.
faring well
εὖ πράσσων.
faring well
τὸ μὲν εὖ πράσσειν ἀκό- ρεστον ἔφυ.
the doing well is insatiable
εὖ γε πράξας.
having fared well
κα- κοὶ γὰρ εὖ πράσσοντες οὐκ ἀνασχετοί.
for the wicked faring well are not to be endured
καὶ νῦν μὲν ἐς τόδ᾽ ἦμαρ εὖ ῥέπει θεός.
and now up to this day the god inclines well
εὖ τελεῖ θεός.
the god accomplishes well
εὖ ξυντυχόντων
of those who have met with good fortune
cit.note: rebus bene pro- cedentibus.
when things go well.

cit.quote: εἰδὼς εὖ.
knowing well
εὖ τόδ᾽ ἴσθι.
know this well
εὖ γάρ ἴστε.
for know well
εὖ τόδ᾽ ἴσθι.
know this well
εὖ νῦν τόδ᾽ ἴσθι.
now know this well
εὖ γὰρ σαφῶς τόδ᾽ ἴστε.
for know this well and clearly
εὖ γὰρ ἐξεπίσταμαι.
for I know well
εἰδώς γ᾽ εὖ.
knowing well
τοιούδε φωτός πεῖραν εὖ φυλακτέον.
the trial of such a man must be well guarded against
βίον εὖ κυρήσας
having obtained a good life
cit.note: quod schol. exp. εὐτυχήσας, εὖ πράξας: ν. δ. ν. κυρέωhaving been fortunate, having fared well: see under κυρέω .
which the scholiast explains as εὐτυχήσας [having been fortunate], εὖ πράξας [having fared well]: see under κυρέω.

cit.quote: εὖ δὲ πανταχή τελεῖν σοὶ τῶνδε κρίνομεν πέρι.
and we judge that it is well for you to accomplish these things in every way
ἐπεὶ στρα- τὸν εὖ ποδούχει.
since he well commands the army
τὰ δεσποτῶν γὰρ εὖ πε- σόντα θήσομαι.
for I will set the affairs of my masters well when they have fallen
εὖ γὰρ εἴη.
for may it be well
εὖ τοῦτο κἀφρένωσας οὐχ ἥκιστά με.
you have well advised me in this, not least
τὰ δ᾽ εὖ ἐμὸν ἐμὸν κέρδος άέξεται τόδε
and this good thing, my gain, increases
cit.note: ubi Hermannus τὰ δ᾽ εὖ ἔχοντ᾽ ἐμὸν κέρδος αὔξει τόδεand this good thing, my gain, increases .
where Hermann has τὰ δ᾽ εὖ ἔχοντ᾽ ἐμὸν κέρδος αὔξει τόδε [but this well-being increases my gain].

cit.quote: εὖ τὰ τῶν ἐγχωρίων δήμου (δήμου in λαῶν probabiliter mu- tat Heimsoethius) δέδοκται παντελή βουλεύματα.
the counsels of the people of the land have been well decreed to be complete (Heimsoethius probably changes δήμου to λαῶν)
θεοὺς προσειπεῖν εὖ παρασκευάζομαι
I prepare to address the gods well
cit.note: ubi probabilius est aὐwell , quod restituit Paleius.
where αὖ [again] is more probable, which Paleius restored.

cit.quote: εὖ πραπίδων λαχόντα.
having obtained well of the mind
εὖ λέγοντες ἄνδρα.
speaking well of the man
τὸ δ᾽ ὑπερκόπως κλύειν εὖ.
to hear well beyond measure
εὖ γὰρ πρὸς εὖ φανεῖσι προσθήκη πέλοι.
for to those who appear well, well may be an addition
ἀλλ᾽ εὖ νιν ἀ- σπάσασθε.
but greet him well
εὖ γὰρ πέπρακται.
for it has been done well

On the verb εὐθαρσέω [to be of good courage], for which also εὖ θαρσέω [to be of good courage] is written separately, see under εὐθαρσέω.

Said of a bright place from which a view extends widely over the neighborhood.

cit.quote: ἕδραν γὰρ εἶχε παντὸς εὐαγῆ στρατοῦ
For he held the seat of the whole army, bright and pure.
cit.note: ubi schol. καθαράν, κεχωρισμένην · ἢ αὐγάζοντα καὶ ὁρῶνταpure, separated; or shining and seeing . Altera haec interpretatio apta est adiectivo εὐαυγῆbright, gleaming , quod coniectura satis probabili restituit Hemsterhusius apud Musgr. ad Eurip. Suppl. 652, cuius senten- tiam frustra impugnavit Elmsleius ad Eurip. Bacch. 660, recte defendit L. Dindorfius in Thes. vol. 3 p. 2177.

where the scholiast has καθαράν, κεχωρισμένην · ἢ αὐγάζοντα καὶ ὁρῶντα [pure, separated; or shining and seeing]. This second interpretation suits the adjective εὐαυγῆ [bright, gleaming], which Hemsterhuis restored by a sufficiently probable conjecture in Musgrave's note on Euripides Suppl. 652; Elmsley vainly attacked his opinion in his note on Euripides Bacch. 660, and L. Dindorf rightly defended it in the Thesaurus vol. 3 p. 2177.

λαβὼν γὰρ αὐ- τόθηκτον Εὐβοικὸν ξίφος.
For taking a Euboean sword, self-sharpened.
cit.note: Formam trisyllabam ΕὐβοικόςEuboean (pro ΕὐβοϊκόςEuboean ) testatur Herodianus apud Arcad. p. 51, 21, inter hyperdisyllaba in οικοςoikos mo- nens ΕὐβοικόςEuboean , cuius alterum exemplum est apud Eurip. Hel. 767 τὰ Ναυπλίου τ᾽ Εὐβοικὰ πυρπο- λήματαthe Euboean fire-signals of Nauplius , vulgo ΕὐβοϊκάEuboean scriptum.

Herodian in Arcadius p. 51, 21 attests the trisyllabic form Εὐβοικός [Euboean] (for Εὐβοϊκός [Euboean]), among words of more than two syllables ending in οικος [oikos], citing Εὐβοικός [Euboean]; another example is in Euripides Hel. 767 τὰ Ναυπλίου τ᾽ Εὐβοικὰ πυρπολήματα [the Euboean fire-signals of Nauplius], commonly written Εὐβοϊκά [Euboean].

cit.quote: Εὐβοῖδα καμπήν
the Euboean bend
cit.note: ubi ΕὐβοιίδαEuboean in initio trimetri in ΕὐβοῖδαEuboean contractum est, ut Εὐβοῖδα χώρανEuboean land est ap. Soph. Tr. 74: de quo v. Thes. vol. 3 p. 2201.
where Εὐβοιίδα [Euboean] at the beginning of a trimeter is contracted to Εὐβοῖδα [Euboean], as Εὐβοῖδα χώραν [Euboean land] is in Sophocles Trach. 74; on which see the Thesaurus vol. 3 p. 2201.

cit.quote: καὶ νῦν Ὀρέστης, ἦν γάρ εὐβόλως ἔχων, ἔξω κομίζων ὀλεθρίου πηλοῦ πόδα.
And now Orestes, for he was fortunate in his throw, carrying his foot out of the destructive mud.
cit.note: metaphora ab aleatoribus sumta. Sic Porsonus pro εὐβούλωςwith good counsel .
metaphor taken from dice-players. Thus Porson for εὐβούλως [with good counsel].

cit.quote: μηδ᾽ αὐθαδίαν εὐβουλίας ἀμείνον᾽ ἡγήσῃ ποτέ.

sense.def: vitiose pro εὐβόλωςfortunately in casting , quod v.

εὐγενὲς γύναι.

form.gloss: gifted with a good tongue, i.e. eloquent

cit.quote: ήβῶντα δ᾽ εὐγλώσσῳ φρενί.
in the bloom of youth with an eloquent mind.
μηδέ μοι φθονήσης εὐγμάτων.
and do not begrudge me my prayers.
ἐμῶν ἀκούσασ᾽ εὐγμάτων.
having heard my prayers.
τρόμος μ᾿ ὑφέρπει κλύουσαν εὐγμά- των.
trembling creeps over me as I hear the prayers.
Κῦρος, εὐδαίμων ἀνήρ.
Cyrus, a blessed man.
ἄναξ Ἀτρείδης πρέσβυς εὐδαίμων ἀνήρ.
Lord Atreides, an old and blessed man.
οἴκοι μένειν χρὴ τὸν καλῶς εὐδαί- μονα.
He who is truly blessed should remain at home.
ὦ μέγ᾽ εὔδαιμον κόρη
O greatly blessed maiden
cit.note: ubi M a m. pr. εὐδαίμωνblessed , sed superscripta a m. sec. littera o. In apogr. pluribus εὐδαῖμονblessed contra regulam Herodiani apud Choerob. in Theodos. p. 438, 30.

where M in the first hand has εὐδαίμων [blessed], but with the letter o written above by a second hand. In several copies εὐδαῖμον [blessed] is found, contrary to the rule of Herodian in Choeroboscus on Theodosius p. 438, 30.

cit.quote: οὐδεὶς ἀκούει ταῦτα τῶν εὐ- δαιμόνων.
No one of the blessed hears these things.
ξένοισιν ὧδ᾽ εὐδαίμοσιν.
to strangers so blessed.
οὐχ ἧσσον εὐδάκρυτά μοι λέγεις τάδε.
You tell me things no less lamentable.
οὕτω γὰρ ἄν σοι δαῖτες ἔννομοι βροτῶν κτιζοίατ᾽ · εἰ δὲ μὴ, παρ᾿ εὐδείπνοις ἔσει ἄτιμος ἐμπύροισι κνισωτοῖς χθονός.
For thus would lawful feasts of mortals be established for you; but if not, you will be dishonored among the savory burnt offerings of the earth.
cit.note: de mortuis quibus sacrificia offeruntur. Schol. ἄτιμος ἐμπύροισιdishonored among the burnt offerings (codex ἐν πυροῖσι) κνισωτοῖς ἔσῃ παρ᾿ εὐδείπνοις χθονός, ὅ ἐστι παρὰ κατοιχομένοις δείπνῳ τιμώμενος. οὕτως τὸ ἑξῆς, τῶν ἄλ- λων νεκρῶν μεταλαμβανόντων ἐναγισμῶν σὺ ἄτιμος ἔσῃin the wheat) with savory feasts you will be among the good feasts of the earth, that is, honored with a feast among the departed. Thus the sequence: while the other dead receive offerings, you will be dishonored . Etym. Μ αἰώρα: ἑορτὴ Ἀθηνᾶς, ἣν κα- λοῦσιν εὔδειπνον · λέγεται γὰρ Ἠριγόνην τὴν Αἰ- γίσθου καὶ Κλυταιμνήστρας θυγατέρα σὺν Τυνδά- ρεῳ τῷ πάππῳ ἐλθεῖν ἈθήναζεM αἰώρα [the Swing festival]: a festival of Athena, which they call εὔδειπνον [the good feast]; for it is said that Erigone, daughter of Aegisthus and Clytemnestra, came to Athens with her grandfather Tyndareus . Similiter He- sychius s.v. εὐδείπνοιςto the good feasts . Photius p. 28, 14 εὐδεί- πνους: τὰς τοῖς τεθνεῶσιν ἐπιφερομένας χοάς. εὔδειπνοι δαῖτεςthe good feasts: the libations brought to the dead. good feasts est apud Eurip. Med. 200. Ex his colligi potest εὐδείπνοιςgood feasts apud Aeschylum ad- iective, ἐμπύροισιburnt offerings substantive dictum esse.

of the dead to whom sacrifices are offered. Schol. ἄτιμος ἐμπύροισι [dishonored among the burnt offerings] (codex ἐν πυροῖσι [in the wheat]) κνισωτοῖς ἔσῃ παρ᾿ εὐδείπνοις χθονός [you will be with the savory feasts of the earth], that is, honored with a feast among the departed. Thus the sequence: while the other dead receive offerings, you will be dishonored. Etym. Μ αἰώρα [the Swing festival]: a festival of Athena, which they call εὔδειπνον [the good feast]; for it is said that Erigone, daughter of Aegisthus and Clytemnestra, came to Athens with her grandfather Tyndareus. Similarly Hesychius s.v. εὐδείπνοις [to the good feasts]. Photius p. 28, 14 εὐδείπνους [the good feasts]: the libations brought to the dead. εὔδειπνοι δαῖτες [good feasts] is in Eurip. Med. 200. From these it can be gathered that εὐδείπνοις [good feasts] in Aeschylus is used adjectivally, ἐμπύροισι [burnt offerings] substantivally.

cit.quote: πεπλήγμεθ᾽, εὔδηλα γάρ.
We have been struck; for it is manifest.
πόλις δ᾽ ἐν εὐδίᾳ.

πρῶτα μὲν εὐδοκίμου στρατιᾶς ἀπεφαινόμεθα.

ἀλκὴν δ᾽ εὐδόκιμον (Aeschyli) Μαρά- θώνιον ἄλσος ἂν εἴποι.
And the Marathonian grove would speak of the glorious might (of Aeschylus).
Τροίας ἀναστατή- ρας εὐδόξῳ φρενί
having overthrown Troy with glorious mind
ἀφύλακτον εὑδήσουσι πᾶσαν εὐφρόνην.
They will sleep unguarded all night.
θαυμαστός λόχος εὕ- δει γυναικῶν.
A wondrous ambush of women sleeps.
εὕδοιτ᾽ ἄν.
You would sleep.
εὕδουσα γὰρ φρὴν ὄμμασιν λαμπρύνεται.
For the sleeping mind is brightened by the eyes.
εὕδεις;
Are you sleeping?
εὑ- δόντων ὕπερ ἐγρηγορὸς φρούρημα.

εύ- δοντι καὶ στείχοντι καὶ καθημένῳ.

ἰὼ μάκαρες εὔεδροι.

εὐειδὴς ἀνήρ.
a beautiful man
δύο γυναῖκ᾽ εὐείμονε.

εὔελπίς εἰμι τῶνδέ σ᾽ ἐκ δεσμῶν ἔτι λυ- θέντα μηδὲν μεῖον ἰσχύσειν Διός.
I have good hope that you, released from these bonds, will be no less strong than Zeus.
ἐστὶ δ᾽ οὐκ εὐέξοδον
It is not easy to exit.
cit.note: i.e. non facile est exire.
i.e. it is not easy to exit.

ύφασμα εὐήτριον ·

cit.quote: εὐ- θαρσὴς ἐγώ.
I am of good courage.
πατέρ᾽ εὐθαρση.

so that no house may thrive without you.

μῆλά τ᾽ τ᾽ εὐθενοῦντα.
and the flocks thriving
ἔχει δέ καινοπηγές εὔθετον σάκος

cit.note: ubi Μ εὔκυκλονM: well-rounded cum γρ. εὔθετον, ἵν᾽ ἡ εὐ- βάστακτον · θεῖναι γὰρ τὸ ἀναλαβεῖν λέγουσιν Ἀτ · τικοί, ἀσπίδ᾽ εὐκυκλονvariant: well-placed, where the gloss easy to carry; for the Attic writers say to place for to take up; well-rounded shield est v. 590.

where M has εὔκυκλον [well-rounded] with the variant εὔθετον [well-placed], where the gloss εὐβάστακτον [easy to carry] is given; for the Attic writers say θεῖναι [to place] for ἀναλαβεῖν [to take up]; ἀσπίδ᾽ εὐκυκλον [well-rounded shield] is at line 590.

easy to catch by hunting; improperly

πόθεν ἕξεις ὁμοίας χειρὸς εὔθοινον γέρας;

εὐθυ- μῶν ἐμέ.
cheering me

cit.quote: τοσαῦτ᾽ ἔλεξε κάρθ᾽ ὑπ᾽ εὐθύμου φρενός
