ἔθυσεν αὑτοῦ παῖδα, φιλτάτην ἐμοὶ ὠδῖνα.
he sacrificed his own child, the dearest offspring to me.
ὤζεις; ὑπνώσσεις;
Are you crying out? Are you sleeping?
cit.note: ubi audito chori ὠγμῷcry of lament , qui notatur per παρεπιγραφὴν ὠγμόςstage direction: a cry of lament , Clytaemnestra quaerit Schol. ὡς παρὰ τὸ αἴ αἴ αἰάζειν, οὕτω παρὰ τὸ ὦ ὤ ὤζεινjust as from αἴ αἴ [alas, alas] comes αἰάζειν [to cry alas], so from ὦ ὤ [oh, oh] comes ὤζειν [to cry oh] . Aliorum exempla v. in Thes. vol. 8 p. 2000.

where, having heard the chorus's ὠγμῷ [cry of lament], which is marked by the stage direction ὠγμός [a cry of lament], Clytaemnestra asks: Schol. ὡς παρὰ τὸ αἴ αἴ αἰάζειν, οὕτω παρὰ τὸ ὦ ὤ ὤζειν [just as from αἴ αἴ [alas, alas] comes αἰάζειν [to cry alas], so from ὦ ὤ [oh, oh] comes ὤζειν [to cry oh]]. For examples of others see Thes. vol. 8 p. 2000.

form.gloss: oh! (exclamation of one shouting or calling)

sense.def: an exclamation of one shouting or calling

cit.quote: εὕδοιτ᾽ ἂν, ὠὴ, καὶ καθευδουσῶν τί δεῖ;
You would be sleeping, oh! and what need is there of sleeping women?
cit.note: Non legitur apud Sophoclem neque apud comicos, sed aliquoties apud Euripidem: v. Thes, vol. 8 p. 2000.
It is not found in Sophocles nor in the comic poets, but several times in Euripides: see Thes. vol. 8 p. 2000.

cit.quote: ἔξω δόμων τε καὶ πάτρας ὠθεῖν ἐμέ.
to thrust me out of the house and fatherland.
παῖδες πατρὸς Ὠκεανοῦ.
children of father Oceanus.
οὐ γάρ ποτ᾽ ἐρεῖς ὡς Ὠκεανοῦ φίλος ἔστι βεβαιότερός σοι.
For you will never say that a friend of Oceanus is more steadfast to you.
παρ᾽ Ωκεανοῦ πατρὸς ἄσβεστον πόρον.
the unquenchable stream from father Oceanus.
χαλκοκέραυνόν τε παρ᾽ Ὠκεανῷ λίμνην.
and the bronze-thundering lake by Oceanus.
παλαιγενή γὰρ λέγω παρβασίαν ὠκύποινοv.
For I speak of an ancient transgression, swift in punishment.
cit.note: Schol. τὴν ὀξέως μετελθοῦσαν αὐτόνthe one who swiftly pursued him .
Schol. τὴν ὀξέως μετελθοῦσαν αὐτόν [the one who swiftly pursued him].

cit.quote: πατέρ᾽ ἀντιάσασα πρὸς ὠκύπορον πόρθμευμ᾽ ἀχέων.
having come to my father at the swift-passing ferry of sorrows.
cit.note: De fluvio celeriter fluente.
Of a river flowing swiftly.

cit.quote: νῆες ὡς ὠκύπτεροι ἥκουσι.
ships like swift-winged ones have come.
καὶ τῶνδε καιρὸν ὅστις ὤκιστος λαβέ.
and take the swiftest opportunity of these things.
ἄραρεν ἥδε γ᾽ ὠλένη δυσεκλύτως.
this arm is fitted hard to loosen.
Ὤλενος: πόλις Ἀχαΐας καὶ Αἰτωλίας, θηλυκώς λεγομένη.
Olenus: a city of Achaea and Aetolia, spoken of in the feminine gender.
“τὴν αἰπεινὴν Ζαθέαν (τ᾽ addit cod. Paris.) Ὤλενον.”
"steep and sacred Olenus" (the Paris codex adds τ᾽ [and]).
πέφρικα τὰν ὠλεσίοικον θεόν.
I shudder at the house-destroying goddess.
ὠμηστὴς λέων.
a raw-flesh-eating lion.
ὠμοδακής σ᾽ ἄγαν ἵμερος ἐξοτρύνει.
a cruel-biting desire urges you too much.
ὠμοδρόπων νομίμων προπάροιθεν.
before the lawful rites of unripe-plucked maidens.
cit.note: De puellis quibus erepta ab hostibus virginitas est ubi schol. ὑπὸ τῶν ὠμῶς αὐτῶν δρεπομένων τὴν ήβην πρὸ τῶν νομίμων γάμωνby those who cruelly pluck their youth before lawful marriage .
Of girls whose virginity was taken by enemies, where the scholium says: ὑπὸ τῶν ὠμῶς αὐτῶν δρεπομένων τὴν ήβην πρὸ τῶν νομίμων γάμων [by those who cruelly pluck their youth before lawful marriage].

cit.quote: ὠμολίνου μακροὶ τόνοι.
long cords of raw flax.
κίον᾿ οὐρανοῦ τε καὶ χθονός ὤμοιν (sic ex apogr. pro ὤμοις) ἐρείδων.
resting on his shoulders (thus from the copy for ὤμοις [shoulders]) the pillar of heaven and earth.
ὠμὸν, οὔτι παρθένων ἐπώνυμον, φρόνημα.
a cruel spirit, not named after maidens.
ὠμοί τε δούλοις πάντα καὶ παρὰ στάθμην.
and cruel in all things to slaves and beyond measure.
δι᾽ ὠμὰν ἔριν αἱματηράν.
through cruel bloody strife.
cit.note: Sic Klausenus pro αιωμαναιρειν. ἔρινto take away strife ex annotatione scholiastae restituerat Hermannus, qui διώκειν ἔρινto pursue strife scripsit.
Thus Klausen for αιωμαναιρειν. ἔριν [to take away strife]. Hermann had restored ἔριν [strife] from the scholiast's note, and wrote διώκειν ἔριν [to pursue strife].

cit.quote: ὠμῇ ξὺν ὀργῇ.
with cruel anger.
Σφίγγ᾽ ὠμόσιτον.
the raw-flesh-eating Sphinx.
ὡς ὠμοφρόνως δαίμων ἐνέβη Περσῶν γενεᾷ.
how with cruel mind the deity entered the race of the Persians.
ὠμόφρων σίδαρος.
cruel-minded iron.
λύκος γὰρ ὥστ᾽ ὠμόφρων.
for like a cruel-minded wolf.
τίς ἂν φίλους ὠνοῖτο τοὺς κεκτημένους,
who would buy friends who are already owned?
cit.note: ubi ὠνοῖτοhe might buy Turnebus. ὤνοιτο ΜM has ὤνοιτο , quasi ὄνοιτοhe might blame voluerit, quod coniecit Boissonadius.
where Turnebus reads ὠνοῖτο [he might buy]. M has ὤνοιτο, as if he had intended ὄνοιτο [he might blame], which Boissonade conjectured.

cit.quote: ὥρα δ᾽ ἐμπόρους μεθιέναι (correxi καθιέναι) ἄγκυραν.
and it is time for merchants to let down the anchor (I corrected καθιέναι [to let down]).
καὶ νυκτίσεμνα δεῖπν᾽ ἐπ᾿ ἐσχάρᾳ πυρὸς ἔθυον ὥραν οὐδενὸς κοινὴν θεῶν.
and they sacrificed night-honored meals on the hearth of fire, a season shared by none of the gods.

sense.def: tempus aetatis florentis, aetas iuvenilis, iuventutis flos.
the time of blooming age, youthful age, the flower of youth

cit.quote: στεῖχει δ᾽ ἴουλος ἄρτι διὰ παρηίδων, ὥρας φυούσης.
And the down is just now coming over his cheeks, as the season of youth blooms.
ὥραν ἐχούσας τήνδ᾽ ἐπίστρεπτον βροτοῖς.
having this season that turns mortals back.
δενδρῶτις ὥρα δ᾽ ἐκ νοτίζοντος γάμου τέλειός ἐστι.
The tree-bearing season from the moistening marriage is complete.
λοιβάς Διὸς μὲν πρῶτον ὡραίου γάμου, τὴν δευτέραν δὲ κρᾶσιν ἥρωσιν νέμω,
First I pour libations to Zeus of the ripe marriage, and the second mixing I assign to the heroes,
cit.note: i.e. coniugii matura aetate initi.
i.e. entered into at the mature age for marriage.

sense.def: Orithyia inscripta fuit Aeschyli tragoedia, cuius unum superest fragmentum (280).
A tragedy of Aeschylus was entitled Orithyia, of which one fragment (280) survives.
sense.note: Eiusdem nominis tragoediam scripsisse Sophoclem non potest colligi ex verbis Ioannis Siceliotae ad Aeschyli fragm. 280 allatis: de quo dixit Wilamowitzius in Herme vol. 10 p. 334. Fuit autem Orithyia Erechthei filia, quam ex Attica abreptam Boreas in Thraciam abduxit ex eaque suscepit Zeten et Calain: v. Thes. vol. 8 p. 2064.

That Sophocles wrote a tragedy of the same name cannot be inferred from the words of John Siceliotes cited on Aeschylus frag. 280: on this Wilamowitz spoke in Hermes vol. 10 p. 334. Orithyia was the daughter of Erechtheus, whom Boreas snatched from Attica and carried off to Thrace, and by him she bore Zetes and Calais: see Thes. vol. 8 p. 2064.

sense.def: particula praepositionis, adverbii et coniunctionis significationem habet: unde triginta eius significationes finxerunt grammatici quidam, quae revera ad paucas redeunt, ut in Thes. ostensum est vol. 8 p. 2077-2106. Praepositionis (ad, in), quae cum accusativo construitur, nulla apud Aeschylem exempla reperiuntur, sunt vero non pauca adverbii et coniunctionis.

It has the force of a preposition, adverb, and conjunction: hence certain grammarians have invented thirty meanings for it, which in fact reduce to a few, as is shown in Thes. vol. 8 p. 2077-2106. No examples of the preposition (to, into), which is construed with the accusative, are found in Aeschylus, but there are not a few of the adverb and conjunction.
ὡςas, how, that, so that, since adverbium, duarum vel personarum vel rerum comparationi serviens, Latinis respondet particulis, ut, sicut, velut, quemadmodum, tanquam.
ὡς as an adverb, serving for comparison of two persons or things, corresponds to the Latin particles ut, sicut, velut, quemadmodum, tanquam.

cit.quote: δράκοντα δ᾽ ὡς τις τέκνων ὑπερδέδοικεν – πελειάς.
But as someone fears a serpent for her children – a dove.
δακὼν δὲ στόμιον ὡς νεοζυγὴς πῶλος.
Biting the bit like a newly yoked colt.
λεόντων ὡς ῎Αρη δεδορκότων.
of lions glaring like Ares.
ὡς δράκων βοᾷ.
as a serpent cries.
εἴρξει νεοσσῶν ὡς δράκοντα δύσχιμον.
he will keep out the hostile serpent from the nestlings.
ὡς θεός.
as a god.
ὡς τις ἥλιος.
like some sun.
ὡς ἐν γραφαῖς.
as in paintings.
1436 ὡς τὸ πρόσθε.
1436 as before.
ὡς δὲ δαίμονες εὑδήσουσιν.
but as divinities they will sleep.
τρόπος δὲ θηρὸς ὡς νεαιρέτου.
the manner of a newly caught beast.
ὡς δὲ φάρμακον τεύχουσα.
as one preparing a drug.
ὡς ἀγύρτρια.
as a begging priestess.
ὡς ὄρνις.
as a bird.
και θάρμαθ᾽ ὡς τις ἐκπέμψας.
and as one sending out charms.
ἐπαίσθην δ᾽ ὡς διανταίῳ βέλει.
I was struck as by a piercing bolt.
ὡς κύων νεβρόν ἐκματεύομεν.
like a hound we track the fawn.
θρασύς ταγοῦχος ὡς ἀνήρ.
a bold man holding command.
ἐκζέουσ᾽ ὡς καρδίαν ἀλεκτόρων.
boiling over as the heart of cocks.
ἑσμὸς ὡς πελειάδων.
a swarm as of doves.
λυκοδίωκτον ὡς δάμαλιν.
as a heifer chased by wolves.
σκάφος στρέβλαισι ναυτικαῖσιν ὡς προσηγμένον.
a hull brought in by nautical windlasses.
πάρεστι δ᾽ ἔργον ὡς ἔπος.
the deed is present as the word.
διψὰς ὡς κόνις,
thirsty as dust,
cit.note: ut correxi pro δόσως κόνιςdust as a gift .
as I corrected for δόσως κόνις.

cit.quote: ὡς θεοῖς Ὀλυμπίοις.
as to the Olympian gods.

sense.def: ὡςas, how, that, so that, since rei comparatae postpositum cum accentu scribitur
ὡς placed after the thing compared is written with an accent

cit.quote: βακχᾷ πρὸς ἀλκὴν Θυιὰς ὥς.
a Bacchant for strength, like a Thyiad.
δοῦλον ὥς. ὥς.
as a slave. as.
παιδὸς νέας ὥς.
as of a young girl.
τοξότης τις ὥς.
like some archer.
βωμὸν ὡς.
as an altar.
φελλοὶ δ᾽ ὡς ἄγουσι δίκτυον.
and corks as they guide the net.
ποταμὸς ὥς.
as a river.
ἄραχνος ὥς.
as a spider.
ἔχιδνα δ᾽ ὡς.
and as a viper.
ἀσχέδωρος ὥς.
as a wild boar.
κακὸς δ᾽ ἰατρὸς ὥς τις.
but a bad physician, as someone.
ἵππος χαλινῶν ὡς κατασθμαίνων μένει.
a horse panting through the bit remains.
σμῆνος ὡς ἐκλέλοιπεν μελισσᾶν.
the swarm of bees has left.

sense.def: ὡςas, how, that, so that, since quam post comparativum pro ἤor, than positum est
ὡς is used for quam after a comparative instead of ἤ

cit.quote: μή μου προκήδου μᾶσσον ὡς ἐμοὶ γλυκύ,
do not care for me more than is sweet to me,
cit.note: quod similibus exemplis ego in Annot. Oxon, p. 85 et Hermannus in Annot. p. 113. defendimus, quae tamen parum certa sunt, quum ὡςas, how, that, so that, since ex ὧνof which, whose corruptum esse possit, quod aliis in locis intactum reliquerunt librarii. Hinc apud Aeschylum scripsi μᾶσσον ὧν ἐμοὶ γλυκύmore than which is sweet to me , nisi praeferenda lenissima Elmsleii correetio μασσό νως ἢ μοί γλυκύmore than which is sweet to me . Minus probabile est ἢ ὡςor as cum synizesi, quod ex apographo aliquo memorat Turnebus.

which I defended with similar examples in Oxford Annotations p. 85 and Hermann in Annotations p. 113, though these are not very certain, since ὡς [as] could be corrupted from ὧν [of which], which the scribes left untouched in other places. Hence in Aeschylus I wrote μᾶσσον ὧν ἐμοὶ γλυκύ [greater than which is sweet to me], unless Elmsley's very gentle correction μασσό νως ἢ μοί γλυκύ [greater than sweet to me] is to be preferred. Less probable is ἢ ὡς [or as] with synizesis, which Turnebus mentions from some copy.

sense.def: ὡςas, how, that, so that, since , praecedente τοιόσδε, τόσοςsuch, so great .

cit.quote: ἀλλ᾽ οὔτι πω τοιόνδ᾽ ἐναργὲς εἰδόμην, ὡς τῆς πάροιθεν εὐφρόνης.
but never yet did I see such a clear vision as that of the former night.
τραυμάτων μὲν εἰ τόσων ἐτύγχανεν ἀνὴρ ὅδ᾽, ὡς πρὸς οἶκον ὠχετεύετο φάτις.
if this man had received so many wounds, as the report was channeled to the house.
οὐδὲν ἀγγέλων σθένος ὡς αὐτὸν αὐτῶν (αὐτὸς αὐτὸν Μ: αὐτοῦ Schuetzius, αὐτῶν Turnebus) ἄνδρα πεύθεσθαι πάρα (sic Hermannus pro πέρι),
no strength of messengers as to learn from the man himself (himself M: his Schuetz, of them Turnebus) is possible (thus Hermann for concerning),
cit.note: quod schol. exp. οὐ τοσοῦτον ἰσχύει εἰπεῖν ἄγγελος ὡς ὁ αὐτόπτης. οὐδὲν ὡςa messenger does not have as much power to speak as an eyewitness. nothing as igitur cum infinitivo dictum est ut οὐδὲν οἷονnothing like cum infinitivo, quod comparavit Blomfieldus, allatis exemplis Aristophanis Av. 966 οὐδὲν οἷόν ἐστ᾽ ἀκοῦσαι τῶν ἐπῶνthere is nothing like hearing the words et Platonis Gorg. p. 447 c. οὐδὲν οἷον τὸ αὐτὸν ἐρωτᾶνthere is nothing like asking him oneself . quibus Scholefieldus addidit Demosth. p. 529 οὐδὲν γὰρ οἷον ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ τοῦ νόμουfor there is nothing like hearing the law itself .

which the scholiast explains: οὐ τοσοῦτον ἰσχύει εἰπεῖν ἄγγελος ὡς ὁ αὐτόπτης [a messenger is not so able to speak as the eyewitness]. Therefore οὐδὲν ὡς [nothing as] is said with the infinitive like οὐδὲν οἷον [nothing like] with the infinitive, which Blomfield compared, adducing examples from Aristophanes Av. 966 οὐδὲν οἷόν ἐστ᾽ ἀκοῦσαι τῶν ἐπῶν [there is nothing like hearing the words] and Plato Gorg. p. 447 c. οὐδὲν οἷον τὸ αὐτὸν ἐρωτᾶν [there is nothing like asking oneself]. To these Scholefield added Demosth. p. 529 οὐδὲν γὰρ οἷον ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ τοῦ νόμου [for there is nothing like hearing the law itself].

cit.quote: οὕτως ὡς ἐφ᾽ ἑκάστη διεκλήρωσεν Δαναός.
so as Danaus assigned by lot to each.
cit.note: Praecedente oὕτωςthus, so .
Preceded by οὕτως [thus].

cit.quote: ὡς δ᾽ ὑπέραυχα βάζουσιν -, τώς νιν Ζεὺς νεμέτωρ ἐπίδοι κοταίνων.
but as they speak arrogantly -, so may Zeus the avenger look upon them with wrath.
cit.note: Respondente in altero sententiae membro τώςthus, so .
With τώς [thus] answering in the other member of the sentence.

sense.def: ὡςas, how, that, so that, since relative positum, quomodo, qua ratione.
ὡς used relatively, how, in what way.

cit.quote: ὡς δ᾽ ἥμαρτες οὔτ᾽ ἐμοὶ λέγειν καθ᾽ ἡδονὴν σοί τ᾽ ἄλγος.
but as you erred, it is not for me to speak for pleasure, nor for you for pain.
ἀκούσαθ᾽ ὡς σφας νηπίους ὄντας τὸ πρὶν ἔννους ἔθηκα.
hear how I made them, who were before foolish, wise.
ἐσορᾷς μ᾿ ὡς ἔκδικα πάσχω.
you see me how I suffer unjustly.
λέγοιμ᾽ ἂν εἰδὼς εὐ τὰ τῶν ἐναντίων, ὥς τ᾽ ἐν πύλαις ἕκαστος εἴληχεν πάλον.
I could speak knowing well the affairs of the enemy, how each at the gates has obtained his lot.
ὁρᾶτέ μ᾿ ὡς παρεσκευασμένος – προσίζομαι.
you see me how prepared – I sit as suppliant.
ἀκούσαθ᾿ ὡς ἔλεξα τῆς ἐμῆς περὶ ψυχῆς,
hear how I spoke concerning my life,
cit.note: nisi ἠκούσαθ᾽ ὧνyou heard of which scribendum, ut ib. 46 ὧνof which, whose in ὡςas, how, that, so that, since corruptum.
unless ἠκούσαθ᾽ ὧν [you heard of which] is to be written, as at line 46 ὧν [of which] was corrupted into ὡς [as].

cit.quote: λέξαι τε λάχη τὰ κατ᾿ ἀνθρώπους ὡς ἐπινωμᾷ στάσις ἀμά. μά.
and to tell the lots among men how the faction distributes them. .
γένος τε τοὐμὸν ὡς ἔχει πεύσει τάχα.
and you will soon learn how my race fares.
θαυμάζομέν σου γλῶσσαν ὡς θρασύστομος.
we marvel at your tongue, how bold-mouthed.
μάθ᾿ ὡς ὀρθῶς ἐρῶ.
learn how rightly I will speak.
γνώσει δὲ τάδ᾽ ὡς ἔτυμα.
and you will know that these things are true.

sense.def: ὡςas, how, that, so that, since in adverbiali enuntiatione, ut, qua ratione.
ὡς in an adverbial clause, as, in what way.

cit.quote: νῦν δ᾽ ὡς ὁ μάντις φησίν.
but now as the seer says.
ὡς ἐμοὶ δοκεῖ.
as it seems to me.
ὡς τὰ γράμματα λέγει.
as the letters say.
ὡς ἐφίεσαι.
as you command.
ὡς ἕκαστος ἦν τεταγμένος.
as each was stationed.
ὡς ὁ φρυκτὸς ἀγγέλλων πρέπει.
as the beacon announcing shines.
ὡς θέλει τόδ᾽ ἄγχιστον Ἀπίας γαίας μονόφρουρον ἕρκος.
as he wishes this nearest single-guarded fence of the Apian land.
ὡς ἕκαστος ἔσπασεν τύχης πάλον.
as each drew the lot of fortune.
ἔπραξεν ὡς ἔκρανεν.
he did as he accomplished.
ὡς νῦν τὸ σὸν δὴ (τρέω).
as now your (I tremble).
ὡς ἐπλήθυον λόγοι.
as the words were multiplying.
ὡς χρῆν.
as it was necessary.
πράξασαν ὡς ἔπραξεν.
having done as she did.
ὡς χρή.
as is necessary.
ὡς ὁρᾷς.
as you see.
χρῆν τάδ᾽ ὡς ἐπράξαμεν.
it was necessary that these things as we did.
ὡς νόμος βροτοῖς ἐστί.
as is the custom for mortals.
ὡς αὐτὴ λέγει.
as she herself says.
ὡς τοὔνειρον ἐννέπει τόδε.
as this dream tells.
ὡς ἐπεικάσαι πάθη πάρεστιν.
as it is possible to conjecture the sufferings.
ὡς λόγος τις.
as some story.
ἴτων πάλῳ λαχόντες, ὡς νομίζεται.
let them go having obtained by lot, as is customary.
ὡς λέγεις σύ.
as you say.
ὡς ἀκούσει.
as you will hear.
ὡς ἐπίσταμαι.
as I know.
ὡς ἐπήλυδας πρέπει.
as is fitting for newcomers.
ὡς λόγος.
as the story goes.
ὡς ἐγὼ σέθεν κλύω.
as I hear from you.
ὡς λέγει γέρον γράμμα.
as the ancient writing says.
τούτω στάσιν τιν᾿ ὡς ἐγὼ ᾿δόκουν ὁρᾶν τεύχειν ἐν ἀλλήλαισι.
these two I thought I saw making some faction against each other.
cit.note: ubi τεύχεινto make, to build pro ἔτευχονI was making, I was building dictum infinitivo ad parenthesin ὡς ἐγὼ ᾿δόκουν ὁρᾶνas I thought I saw relato, cuius negligentiae alterum in hac fabula exemplum est 565 τυτθὰ δ᾽ ἐκφυγεῖν ἄνακτ᾿ αὐτὸν ὡς ἀκούομενand the lord himself escaped a little, as we hear , quod emendavi restituto αὐτόπουνself-footed : de quo dixi in Philologo vol. 13 p. 476 477.

where τεύχειν [to make] is used for ἔτευχον [I was making], the infinitive being referred to the parenthesis ὡς ἐγὼ ᾿δόκουν ὁρᾶν [as I seemed to see], of which negligence there is another example in this play at 565 τυτθὰ δ᾽ ἐκφυγεῖν ἄνακτ᾽ αὐτὸν ὡς ἀκούομεν [and we hear that the king himself escaped a little], which I emended by restoring αὐτόπουν [with his own feet]: about which I spoke in Philologus vol. 13 p. 476 477.

cit.quote: μαντεύομαι γὰρ, ὡς ἂν ἡγῆται θεός.
for I prophesy, as the god may lead.
δυσσεβίας μὲν ὕβρις τέκος ὡς ἐτύμως.
for insolence is truly the child of impiety.
ὡς πλείστοισι.
to as many as possible.
ὡς ῥᾷστα.
as easily as possible.
ὡς ἄριστα.
as best as possible.
ΧΟ. κληδοῦχον Ἥρας φασίν Ἰὼ γενέσθαι. ΒΑ. ἦν ὡς μάλιστα, καὶ φάτις πολλὴ κρατεῖ.
CHORUS: They say Io became the key-holder of Hera. BACCHUS: It was so most certainly, and a widespread report prevails.
949 ὡς τάχιστα.
949 as quickly as possible.
cit.note: Quod etiam ὡς τάχοςas quickly as possible dicitur Sept. 675. Ag. 27. Ch. 889.
Which is also said ὡς τάχος [as quickly as possible] at Sept. 675, Ag. 27, Ch. 889.

sense.def: ὡςas rationem significans, qua quis de aliqua re sentit, vel alteri sentire videtur, ut, tamquam, putans.
ὡς indicating the reason why someone thinks something about a matter, or seems to another to think, as, as if, thinking.

cit.quote: ἐξ ὀμμάτων δ᾽ ἤστραπτε γορ-γωπὸν σέλας, ὡς τὴν Διὸς τυραννίδ᾽ ἐκπέρσων βίᾳ.
From her eyes flashed a Gorgon-like glare, as if she would destroy the tyranny of Zeus by force.
φρονήματος πλέως ὁ μῦθός ἐστιν ὡς ὑπηρέτου θεῶν.
The speech is full of pride, as befits a servant of the gods.
οὐχ ὡς ἄθυμον (sic) Turnebus pro ἄθυμος) οὐδὲ λήματος κάκη.
Not as spiritless (sic) Turnebus for spiritless) nor with cowardice of spirit.
οὐ γὰρ ὡς φυγῇ παιᾶν᾽ ἐφύμνουν.
For they were not chanting the paean as for flight.
βαιά γ᾽ ὡς ἀπὸ πολλῶν.
Small indeed, as from many.
τοιόσδ᾽ ὁ κόμπος τῆς ἀληθείας γέμων οὐκ αἰσχρὸς ὡς γυναικὶ γενναίᾳ λακεῖν.
Such is the boast, full of truth, not shameful for a noble woman to utter.
πειρᾶσθέ μου γυναικὸς ὡς ἀφράσμονος.
You are testing me as if I were a foolish woman.
εἰς τὸ πᾶν ἔπραξας ὡς παναίτιος.
You have done everything as the one wholly responsible.
cit.note: ubi probabilius est ὢνbeing , quod restituit Wakefieldus.
where ὢν [being] is more probable, which Wakefield restored.

cit.quote: αἰνῶ δὲ πράσσειν ὡς ὑπευθύνῳ τάδε.
I approve of doing this as one accountable.
κοίμα κελαινοῦ κύματος πικρὸν μένος ὡς σεμνότιμος καὶ ξυνοικήτωρ ἐμοί.
Lull the bitter fury of the dark wave, as you are revered and share my home.
πρὸς σὲ πότερον ὡς ἔτην λέγω;
Do I address you as a kinsman?

sense.def: ὡςas cum participio, ut qui, tanquam.
ὡς with a participle, as one who, as if.

cit.quote: ἐκερτόμησας δήθεν ὡς παῖδ᾽ ὄντα με.
You mocked me, indeed, as if I were a child.
τούτου δ᾽ ἀδελφὸν — ἔξω βαλεῖν ἄθαπτον ὡς ὄντ᾽ ἀναστατήρα Καδμείων χθονός.
And his brother—to cast out unburied, as being the overthrower of the land of the Cadmeans.
λέγουσιν ἡμᾶς ὡς ὀλωλότας.
They say that we are dead.
μαντευόμεσθα τἀνδρὸς ὡς ὀλωλότος.
We are prophesying about the man as if he were dead.
ἕστηκεν ἤδη μήλα προς σφαγάς πυρός, ὡς οὔποτ᾽ ἐλπίσασι τήνδ᾽ ἕξειν χάριν.
The sheep already stand for the slaughter of fire, as for those who never hoped to have this favor.
ἐπιξενοῦμαι ταῦτα δ᾽ ὡς θανουμένη.
I am called a stranger, and these things as one about to die.
φροιμιάζονται γὰρ ὡς τυραννίδος σημεῖα πράσσοντες πόλει.
For they are making preludes, as if performing signs of tyranny for the city.
λέγω δέ σοι τοιαῦτ᾽ ἀπειλεῖν ὡς παρεσκευασμένη ἐκ τῶν ὁμοίων.
I tell you to threaten such things, as one prepared from equal resources.
ὡς ὄντ᾿ Ορέστην τάδε σ᾽ ἐγὼ προσεννέπω;
Do I address you as being Orestes?
δίκην γενέσθαι τῆσδ᾽ ἐπήκοος μένω ὡς ἀμφίβουλος οὖσα θυμοῦσθαι πόλει.
I await the judgment of this case, as one in doubt whether to be angry with the city.
πράσσοις ἂν ὡς Ἀργεῖον ἀντήσας στόλον.
You would act as one who has encountered the Argive expedition.
ὡς καὶ ματαίων ἀνοσίων τε κνωδάλων ἔχοντες ὀργὰς, χρὴ φυλάσσεσθαι κράτος.
Since even vain and unholy beasts have their passions, one must guard against their power.
φρόνει μὲν ὡς ταρβούσα μἀμελεῖν θεῶν.
Think as one who fears to neglect the gods.
ὡς τοίνυν ὄντων τωνδέ σοι μαθεῖν πάρα.
So then, you may learn that these things are so.
στένει πόλισμα γῆθεν ὡς κυκλουμένων.
The city groans from the ground, as if surrounded.
πρὸς τάδ᾽ ὡς οὕτως ἐχόντων τῶνδε σύμβουλοι λόγου τοῦδέ μοι γένεσθε.
Therefore, as these things are so, be my advisors in this matter.
ὡς ὧδ᾽ ἐχόντων χαίροιτ᾽ ἂν, εἰ χαίροιτε.
As things are thus, you would rejoice, if you rejoice.
ἤδη κελεύω τούσδ᾽ ἀπὸ γνώμης φέρειν ψήφον δικαίαν ὡς ἅλις λελεγμένων.
Now I bid them cast a just vote according to their judgment, as enough has been said.

sense.def: ὡςas idem quod ὅτιthat , quod Latini per accusativum cum infinitivo exprimunt.
ὡς the same as ὅτι, which the Latins express by the accusative with infinitive.
sense.note: Cum indicativo construitur in oratione recta.
It is constructed with the indicative in direct speech.

cit.quote: οὐ γάρ ποτ᾽ ἐρεῖς ὡς Ὠκεανοῦ φίλος ἔστι βεβαιότερός σοι.
For you will never say that a friend of Oceanus is more steadfast to you.
σημεῖά σοι τάδ᾽ ἐστὶ τῆς ἐμῆς φρενός, ὡς δέρκεται πλέον τι τοῦ πεφασμένου.
These are signs of my mind, that it sees something beyond what is revealed.
τόδε διεμυθολύγησεν ὡς τὸ κηδεῦσαι καθ᾽ ἑαυτὸν ἀριστεύει μακρῷ.
He told this tale, that marrying within one's own kin is by far the best.
εἶσελθέτω σε μήποθ᾽ ὡς ἐγὼ – θηλύνους γενήσομαι.
Let it never enter your mind that I will become womanish.
μηδέ ποτ᾽ εἴπηθ᾿ ὡς Ζεὺς ὑμᾶς εἰς ἀπρόοπτον πῆμ᾽ εἰσέβαλεν.
And never say that Zeus cast you into unforeseen ruin.
δείξαθ᾽ ὡς φιλοπόλεις.
Show that you love your city.
οἶδεν ὡς σφε χρὴ τελευτῆσαι μάχη.
He knows that he must die in battle.
πάρεστι δ᾽ εἰπεῖν ἐπ᾿ ἀθλίοισιν ὡς ἐρξάτην πολλὰ μὲν πολίτας.
It is possible to say of the wretched that they did many things to the citizens.
ἴυζ᾽ ἄποτμον δαῖοις δυσαιανῆ βοάν, ὡς πάντα παγκάκως θεοὶ ἔθεσαν.
Raise a mournful, ill-sounding cry for the unfortunate, since the gods have made everything utterly evil.
μεμνῆσθαί τοι πάρα, ὡς Περσίδων πολλὰς μάταν εὔνιδας ἔκτισσαν ἠδ᾽ ἀνάνδρους.
It is possible to remember how they made many Persian women vainly widowed and husbandless.
ἐπίσταμαι μὲν ὡς ἐπ᾿ ἐξειργασμένοις (ἥξω).
I know that I will come upon deeds already done.
ἐπίσταται βροτοῖσιν ὡς, ὅταν κλύδων κακῶν ἐπέλθη, πάντα δειμαίνειν φιλεῖ.
He knows that mortals, when a wave of evils comes, are wont to fear everything.
λέγουσι δ᾽ ὡς σὺ μὲν μέγαν τέκνοις πλοῦτον ἐκτήσω.
They say that you acquired great wealth for your children.
σημανοῦσιν ὄμμασιν βροτῶν, ὡς οὐχ ὑπέρφευ θνητὸν ὄντα χρή φρονεῖν.
They will signal to the eyes of mortals that one must not think beyond mortal bounds.
εὐ λέγοντες ἄνδρα τὸν μὲν ὡς μάχης ἴδρις.
Speaking well of the man as skilled in battle.
μαρτυρεῖ δέ μοι — κόνις τάδε, ὡς οὔτ᾽ ἄναυδος οὔτε σοι δαίων φλόγα ὕλης ὀρείας σημανεῖ.
This dust bears witness to me, that it will signal neither voiceless nor with blazing flame of mountain wood.
μηδ᾽ εἰς Ἑλένην κότον ἐκτρέψης, ὡς ἀνδρολέτειρ᾽, ὡς μία πολλῶν ἀνδρῶν ψυχὰς ὀλέσασ᾽ ἀξύστατον ἄλγος ἔπραξεν.
Do not turn your wrath upon Helen, as if she were the slayer of men, as if she alone destroyed the lives of many men and wrought unbearable grief.
ὡς μὲν ἀναίτιος εἰ τοῦδε φόνου τις ὁ μαρτυρήσων;
Who will testify that you are guiltless of this murder?
γνώσει γέρων ὢν ὡς διδάσκεσθαι βαρύ τῷ τηλικούτῳ.
You will learn, being old, that it is hard for one of your age to be taught.
οἳ γὼ, κατ᾿ ἄκρας εἶπας (sic Bambergerus. ενπασ ' Μ cum puncto supra v) ὡς πορθούμεθα.
Alas, you have spoken to our utter ruin (thus Bamberger; M has ενπασ' with a dot above the v) — how we are being destroyed.
- μαρτυρεῖ δέ μοι φᾶρος τόδ᾽, ὡς ἔβαψεν Αἰγίσθου ξίφος.
This cloak bears witness for me, how Aegisthus' sword dyed it.
ξυντίθησι δὲ παιδὸς μόρον, ὡς αὐτοφόνως ὤλετο.
He is arranging the death of his child, how he perished by his own hand.

sense.def: With the optative in indirect speech.

cit.quote: προυτεθεσπίκει ὡς οὐ κατ᾿ ἰσχὺν οὐδὲ πρὸς τὸ καρτερὸν χρείη, δόλῳ δὲ τοὺς ὑπερσχόντας κρατεῖν.
He had prophesied that not by force nor against the strong should he prevail, but by guile to overcome those who were superior.
ἔλεξε παιδί σῷ Ξέρξη τάδε, ὡς Ἕλληνες οὐ μενοῖεν, ἀλλὰ βιοτον έκσωσοίατο.
He said to your son Xerxes these things, that the Greeks would not remain, but would save their lives.
βοᾷ δὲ χοῦτος γραμμάτων ἐν συλλαβαῖς ὡς οὐδ᾽ ἂν ῎Αρης σφ᾽ ἐκβάλοι πυργωμάτων.
And he shouts in the syllables of letters that not even Ares could cast them from the towers.

sense.def: ὡςas in enuntiatis finalibus et consilium significantibus idem est quod ὅπωςhow .
ὡς in final clauses and those indicating purpose is the same as ὅπως.
sense.note: Cum indicativo temporis praeteriti significat aliquid fieri nos voluisse quod sit irritum.
With the indicative of past tense it signifies that we wished something to happen which was in vain.

cit.quote: εἰ γάρ μ᾽ ὑπὸ γῆν εἰς – Τάρταρον ήκεν, ὡς μήτε θεῶν μήτε τις ἀνδρῶν τοῖσδ᾽ ἐγεγήθει (sic Elmsleius pro ἐπεγήθει).
For if he had sent me beneath the earth to Tartarus, so that neither of gods nor of men would rejoice at these things (thus Elmsley for ἐπεγήθει).

sense.note: Multo frequentius cum coniunctivo, praecedente tempore praesente vel perfecto praesentis significationem habente.
Much more frequently with the subjunctive, when a present or perfect tense with present meaning precedes.

cit.quote: οὔκουν ἐπείξει τῷδε δεσμὰ περιβαλεῖν, ὡς μή σ᾽ ἐλινύοντα προσδερχθῇ πατήρ;
Will you not hasten to cast bonds around him, so that your father may not see you lingering?
ἀκούσαθ᾽, ὡς μάθητε διὰ τέλους τὸ πᾶν.
Listen, so that you may learn the whole matter to the end.
ὡς πολίτας μὴ κακοσπλάγχνους τιθῇς, ἕκηλος ἴσθι.
Be at ease, so that you may not make the citizens ill-hearted.
λιτὰς ἁμετέρας τελεῖθ᾽, ὡς πόλις εὐτυχῇ.
Fulfill our prayers, so that the city may prosper.
τάχυνε δ᾽, ὡς ἄμεμπτος ὦ χρόνου.
Hasten, so that I may be blameless in time.
ἐπεύχομαι δὲ καιρίας πληγῆς τυχεῖν, ὡς ἀσφάδαστος – ὄμμα συμβάλω τόδε.
I pray to obtain a timely blow, so that without convulsion I may close this eye.
ἐμασχαλίσθη δ᾽, ἔθ᾽ ὡς τόδ᾽ εἰδῇς.
He was mutilated, so that you may know this.
Ἀίγισθον ή κρατοῦσα τοὺς ξένους καλειν ὅπως τάχιστ᾽ ἄνωγεν, ὡς σαφέστερον φάτιν πύθηται τήνδε.
The ruling woman ordered Aegisthus to summon the strangers as quickly as possible, so that he might learn this report more clearly.
λέγ᾽ αὖθις, ὡς μάθω σαφέστερον.
Speak again, so that I may learn more clearly.
ἀλλ᾿ αὐτὸν ἐλθεῖν, ὡς ἀδειμάντως κλύῃ, ἄνωχθι.
But bid him come himself, so that he may hear without fear.
στέγαστρον ἀνδρὸς δείξαθ᾽, ὡς ἴδῃ πατήρ.
Show the covering of the man, so that his father may see.
κρῖνον, ὡς τούτοις φράσω.
Decide, so that I may tell these things.
ταύτην τοιαύτην εἶπον, ὡς δηχθῇ λεώς.
I said that she was such, so that the people might be stung.
οὔτοι καμοῦμαί σοι λέγουσα τἀγαθὰ, ὡς μήποτ᾿ εἴπῃς.
I will not weary of telling you the good things, so that you may never say.
ὡς μὴ γένωμαι δμωΐς Αἰγύπτου γένει.
So that I may not become a slave to the race of Aegyptus.
θὲς ὡς ἴδωσι τῆσδ᾽ ἀφίξεως τέκμαρ.
Place it, so that they may see the proof of this arrival.

sense.def: ὡς ἄνas if finale cum coniunctivo.
ὡς ἄν final with the subjunctive.

cit.quote: τοιᾶσδέ τοι ἀμαρτίας σφε δεῖ θεοῖς δοῦναι δίκην, ὡς ἂν διδαχθῇ.
For such a transgression they must pay the penalty to the gods, so that he may be taught.
ἔξελθε πρὸς Λέρνης βαθὺν λειμῶνα –, ὡς ἂν τὸ Δῖον ὄμμα λωφήση πόθου.
Go out to the deep meadow of Lerna, so that the eye of Zeus may cease from longing.
τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους θυμῷ βάλ᾽, ὡς ἂν τέρματ᾽ ἐκμάθῃς ὁδοῦ.
Cast my words into your heart, so that you may learn the ends of the road.
εὐθὺς γενέσθω πορφυρόστρωτος πόρος, ἐς δῶμ᾽ ἄελπτον ὡς ἂν ἡγῆται Δίκη.
Let a purple-strewn path be made at once, so that Justice may lead him to an unexpected house.
σταθώμεν ἐκποδών, ὡς ἂν σαφῶς μάθω.
Let us stand out of the way, so that I may learn clearly.
αἰνῶ δὲ κρύπτειν τάσδε συνθήκας ἐμὰς, ὡς ἂν ληφθῶσιν.
I praise hiding these my agreements, so that they may be caught.
ἀλλ᾽, ὡς ἂν εἰδῆτ᾽, οὐ γὰρ —.
But, so that you may know, for not —.
cit.note: Sic Emperius et Martinus pro ἄλλος ἂν εἰδὴ τοῦτ᾽ ἄρ᾽another would know this then —.
Thus Emperius and Martin for ἄλλος ἂν εἰδὴ τοῦτ᾽ ἄρ᾽ — [another would know this then —].

cit.quote: ὀπάονας Εύμπεμψον, ὡς ἂν τῶν πολισσούχων θεῶν βωμούς ---- εὕρωμεν.
Send attendants, so that we may find the altars of the city-holding gods.
πείσω τὸ κοινὸν, ὡς ἂν εὐμενὲς τιθῶ.
I will persuade the common people, so that I may make them well-disposed.
ὡς ἂν εἰδὼς ἐννέπω σαφέστερον.
So that knowing I may speak more clearly.

sense.def: ὡςas finale cum optativo post tempora praeterita in oratione obliqua
ὡς final with the optative after past tenses in indirect speech

cit.quote: οἱ μὲν θέλοντες ἐκβαλεῖν ἕδρας Κρόνον, ὡς Ζεὺς ἀνάσσοι δῆθεν, οἱ δὲ τούμπαλιν σπεύδοντες, ὡς Ζεὺς μήποτ᾽ ἄρξειεν θεῶν.
Some wishing to cast Cronus from his seat, so that Zeus might rule, forsooth, and others hastening the opposite, so that Zeus might never rule over the gods.
θεοπρόπους ἴαλλεν, ὡς μάθοι τί χρή –.
He sent prophets, so that he might learn what was necessary —.
κληρουμένους δ᾽ ἔλειπον, ὡς πάλῳ λαχὼν ἕκαστος αὐτῶν πρὸς πύλαις ἄγοι λόχον.
They left them casting lots, so that each of them, having obtained by lot, might lead his company to the gates.
δορυσσόους ἔταξαν, ὡς ἔχοιμι τίμιον γέρας.
They appointed spear-bearers, so that I might have an honored prize.
ὡς εἰπεῖν ἔπος.
So to speak.
ὡς τορῶς φράσαι.
To speak clearly.
ὡς ἁπλῷ λόγῳ,
In a word,
cit.note: quod nihil aliud est quam ὡς ἁπλῷ λόγῳ εἰπεῖνto speak in a word .
which is nothing other than ὡς ἁπλῷ λόγῳ εἰπεῖν [to speak in a simple word].

sense.def: ὡςas i.q. ὥστεso that ita ut.
sense.note: Cum infinitivo
With the infinitive

cit.quote: φέρεια δ᾽ ὑφ᾽ αὑτῇ φῶτα Καδμείων ἕνα, ὡς πλεῖστ᾽ ἐπ᾿ ἀνδρὶ τῷδ᾽ ἰάπτεσθαι βέλη.
She carries beneath her one man of the Cadmeans, so that many missiles may be hurled at this man.
τοιάδ᾽ ἐπ᾿ αὐτοὺς ἦλθε συμφορὰ πάθους, ὡς τοῖσδε καὶ δὶς ἀντισηκῶσαι ῥοπῇ.
Such a calamity of suffering came upon them, so as to outweigh these things even twice in the balance.
ὡς στένειν πόλιν Περσών.
So that the city of the Persians may groan.
ὡς μήτε μέγαν μήτ᾽ οὖν νεαρῶν τιν᾽ ὑπερτελέσαι μέγα δουλείας γάγγαμον.
So that neither great nor any of the young may escape the great net of slavery.
ὡς πόλλ᾽ ἀμαυρᾶς ἐκ φρενός μ᾽ ἀναστένειν.
So that many things from my dim mind make me groan.
ὡς μήτ᾽ ἐν ὅρμῳ κύματος Ζάλην ἔχειν, μήτ᾽ ἐξοκεῖλαι πρὸς κραταίλεων χθόνα.
so as neither to have the surge of the wave in the anchorage, nor to run aground on the rocky shore.
ὡς θρασύνεσθαι πλέον.
so as to be more bold.
ὡς μήτε φεύγειν μήτ᾽ ἀμύνεσθαι μόρον.
so as neither to flee nor to ward off death.
ὡς μήτε σωκεῖν μήτε μ᾿ ἀκταίνειν βάσιν.
so as neither to be able to save myself nor to move my step.
ποῦ γὰρ τοσοῦτο κέντρον ὡς μητροκτονεῖν;
For where is there so great a goad as to kill one's mother?
ὡς ταῦτ᾽ Ὀρέστην δρῶντα μὴ βλάβας ἔχειν.
so that Orestes, doing these things, may not suffer harm.
ὡς μή τιν᾿ οἶκον εὐθενεῖν ἄνευ σέθεν.
so that no house may prosper without you.
ἔκραν᾿ ἄνευ κλητῆρος ὡς εἶναι τάδε.
I accomplished these things without a summoner, so that they are as they are.
τῶνδ᾽ ἐφήλωται τορῶς γόμφος διαμπὰξ, ὡς μένειν ἀραρότως.
The bolt has been driven through these things sharply, so as to remain fixed.
καὶ ταῦτα μὲν γράψεσθε πρὸς γεγραμμένοις | πολλοῖσιν ἄλλοις σωφρονίσμασιν πατρός | ἀγνῶθ᾽ ὅμιλον ὡς ἐλέγχεσθαι χρόνῳ,
And write these things in addition to the many other written admonitions of your father, so that the unknown crowd may be tested by time.
cit.note: ubi post versum secundum unum excidisse ver- sum probabiliter coniecit Weilius.
where Weilius plausibly conjectured that one verse was lost after the second verse.

sense.note: Cum indicativo
With the indicative

cit.quote: ὡς (sic corrector: ὧδ᾽ pr. Μ) ἰδεῖν τέλος πάρεστιν οἷον ἤνυσεν κακόν.
so (sic corrector: thus first M) it is possible to see the end of what evil he accomplished.
πρὸς τάδ᾽ ὡς Σούσων μὲν ἄστυ πᾶν κενανδρίαν στένει.
In response to these things, how the whole city of Susa laments the loss of its men.
ὡς ἑκὼν ἐγὼ μαθοῦσιν αὐδῶ κοὐ μαθοῦσι λήθομαι.
As I willingly speak to those who understand, and to those who do not understand I am forgetful.

sense.def: ὡςas i.q. ἐπείwhen , cui Latina respondent quippe, quandoquidem, quoniam, nam.
ὡς i.q. ἐπεί, to which the Latin quippe, quandoquidem, quoniam, nam correspond.

cit.quote: ὡς οὗπιτιμητής γε τῶν ἔργων βαρύς.
since the one who censures these deeds is severe.
στείχωμεν, ὡς κώλοισιν ἀμφίβληστρ᾽ ἔχει.
Let us go, since he has nets around our limbs.
ὡς ἐγὼ εὔελπίς εἰμι.
as I am hopeful.
ὡς τἀποκλαῦσαι ἀξίαν τριβὴν ἔχει.
since it has a delay worthy of lamentation.
πρὸς ταῦτα βούλευ᾽, ὡς ὅδ᾽ οὐ πεπλασμένος ὁ κόμπος.
In response to these things, take counsel, since this boast is not fabricated.
τὸν ἀμόν νυν ἀντίπαλον εὐτυχεῖν θεοὶ δοῖεν, ὡς δικαίως (recte, ut videtur Heimsoethius, διὰ δίκας) πόλεως πρόμαχος ὄρνυται.
May the gods grant my adversary to prosper, since justly (rightly, as Heimsoethius seems to think, through justice) he rises as the city's champion.
cit.note: Legit hoc scholiasta, qui explicat ὅτι δικαίως πρόμαχεται τῆς πόλεωςthat he fights justly for the city : sed nihil causae est cur ΟΣOS , quod Aeschylus scripserat, pro ὡςas potius accipiatur quam pro ös, quod haud dubie restituendum.

The scholiast read this, who explains: ὅτι δικαίως πρόμαχεται τῆς πόλεως [because he rightly fights for the city]: but there is no reason why ΟΣ, which Aeschylus wrote, should be taken as ὡς [as] rather than as ös [who], which is undoubtedly to be restored.

cit.quote: ὡς οὔποτ᾽ ἀνδρὶ τῷδε κηρυκευμάτων μέμψει.
so that you will never blame this man for his messages.
ὡς πᾶσι στέρεσθαι κρατὸς ἦν προκείμενον.
since it was proposed that all be deprived of their heads.
θεός γὰρ οὐκ ἤχθηρεν, ὡς εὔφρων ἔφυ.
For the god did not hate him, since he was well-disposed.
ὡς τοῖς θανοῦσι πλοῦτος οὐδὲν ὠφελεῖ.
since wealth is of no help to the dead.
ὡς κομπάσαι τῷδ᾽ εἰκὸς ἡλίου φάει.
as it is fitting for him to boast in the light of the sun.
τάχυνε δ᾽, ὡς καὶ νυκτός ἅρμ᾽ ἐπείγεται.
Hurry, since the chariot of night is pressing on.
ὡς οὐκ ἔχουσι κῦρος οὐδὲν ἀμφὶ σοῦ.
since they have no authority concerning you.
φοβοῦμαι, νῆες ὡς ὠκύπτεροι ἥκουσι.
I fear that the ships have come swift-winged.

sense.def: ὡςas significatione temporali, quomodo Latini quoque ut particula utuntur, de quo v. Thes. vol. 8 p. 2089.
ὡς with temporal meaning, just as the Latins also use the particle ut, on which see Thes. vol. 8 p. 2089.

cit.quote: οὐδ᾽ ἵκεθ᾽ ὡς κατέκτανεν.
nor did he come as he killed.
ὁ δ᾽ εὐθὺς ὡς ἤκουσεν, πᾶσιν προφωνεῖ τόνδε ναυάρχοις λόγον.
And he, as soon as he heard, proclaimed this word to all the captains.
ὡς δὲ πλῆθος ἐν στενῷ νεῶν ἤθροιστο.
And when the multitude of ships was gathered in the narrow strait.
ὡς γὰρ θεὸς ναῶν ἔδωκε κῦδος Ἕλλησιν μάχης, – ναῶν ἐξέθρωσκον.
For when the god gave the glory of the battle to the Greeks, they leaped from the ships.
λέλυται γὰρ λαὸς ἐλεύθερα βάζειν, ὡς ἐλύθη ζυγὸν ἀλκᾶς.
For the people have been released to speak freely, since the yoke of strength has been loosed.
ἔπειθον οὐδέν᾽ οὐδὲν, ὡς τάδ᾽ ἤμπλακον.
I persuaded no one of anything, since I erred in these things.
ὡς ἐν μιᾷ πληγή κατέφθαρται πολὺς ὄλβος.
since in one blow great prosperity has been destroyed.
ὡς πάντα γ᾽ ἔστ᾽ ἐκεῖνα διαπεπραγμένα.
since all those things have been accomplished.
φεῦ, τῶν Ἀθηνῶν ὡς στένω μεμνημένος.
Alas, how I groan when I remember Athens.
ὡς ἄρ᾽ ἔψευσας φρενῶν Πέρσας.
How you deceived the Persians in your mind.
ὦ δυσπόνητε δαῖμον, ὡς ἄγαν βαρὺς ποδοῖν ἐνήλω παντὶ Περσικῷ γένει.
O toil-worn divinity, how heavily you have leaped with your feet upon the whole Persian race.
ὡς κάρτα μοι σαφῶς ἐδήλωσας κακά.
How clearly you have shown me the evils.
ὦ δαῖμον, ὥς με πόλλ᾽ ἐσέρ-χεται κακὰ ἄλγη.
O divinity, how many evil pains come upon me.
ὡς ὠμοφρόνως δαίμων ἐνέβη Περσῶν γενεᾶ.
How cruelly the divinity has entered the race of the Persians.
ὡς δ᾽ ἐπωλολύξατο ή παντότολμος,
And how she raised the cry of triumph, the all-daring one.
cit.note: ubi per λίανexceedingly explicuit Triclinius.
where Triclinius explained it by λίαν [exceedingly].

cit.quote: ὡς πόλλ᾽ ἐπωπᾷς κἀκποδὼν εὐ κείμενα.
How many things you oversee, and how well they are placed out of the way.
ὥς μοι τὰ μὲν παλαιὰ συγκεκραμένα ἄλγη – ἐμὴν ἤλγυνεν ἐν στέρνοις φρένα.
How the old pains mixed together have grieved my heart in my breast.
ὡς οὐ δικαίως θάνατον ἔχθουσιν βροτοί,
since mortals hate death unjustly.
cit.note: nisi pro ὅτιthat dictum est ab verbo pendens in versibus praecedentibus lecto, quos non apposuit Plutarchus.
unless it is said for ὅτι [that], depending on a verb found in the preceding verses, which Plutarch did not quote.

cit.quote: ὡς δή σύ μοι τύραννος Ἀργείων ἔσει,
since you will be tyrant of the Argives.
cit.note: tu scilicet mihi rex Argivorum eris, ut interpretatur Hermannus. Alia huiusmodi exempla collegerunt Seidler. ad Eur. Iph. T. 1504 et Schneiderus ad Platonis Civ. vol. 1 p. 36.
you, of course, will be king of the Argives for me, as Hermann interprets. Other examples of this kind were collected by Seidler on Eur. Iph. T. 1504 and Schneider on Plato's Republic vol. 1 p. 36.

sense.def: ὡςas (adverbium oxytonum vel secundum grammaticorum veterum sententiam perispomenon ὡςas , de quo v. Thes. vol. 8 p. 2083) i.q. οὕτωςthus sic, frequens apud epicos, picos, rarum apud Atticos, qui eo in certis quibusdam formulis utuntur, οὐδ᾽ ὥς, ἀλλ' ὡςnot even so, but as , aliisque nonnullis.

ὡς (adverb oxytone or, according to the opinion of the ancient grammarians, perispomenon ὡς, on which see Thes. vol. 8 p. 2083) i.q. οὕτως thus, frequent in epic poets, rare in Attic, who use it in certain fixed formulas, οὐδ᾽ ὥς, ἀλλ' ὡς, and a few others.

cit.quote: εἰ πάντα δ᾽ ὡς πράσσοιμεν (sic correxi pro πράσσοιμ᾿ ἄν), εὐθαρσὴς ἐγώ.
And if we should do everything as we might (sic I corrected for we might do), I am confident.
cit.note: Aeschyli unum est exemplum.
There is one example in Aeschylus.

sense.note: Ab hoc diversum est ὡςas accentu notatum ubi rei comparatae postponitur, ut Sept. 498 βακχᾷ πρὸς ἀλκὴν Θυιὰς ὡςlike a Bacchic Thyiad to the fight , aliisque locis supra indicatis.

Different from this is ὡς [as] marked with an accent when it is postponed to the thing compared, as at Sept. 498 βακχᾷ πρὸς ἀλκὴν Θυιὰς ὡς [like a Thyiad for battle], and in other places indicated above.

cit.quote: ἁπλῷ λόγῳ, ὥσπερ δίκαιον πρὸς φίλους οἴγειν στόμα.
In a word, just as it is right to open one's mouth to friends.
μοχθηρὸν, ὥσπερ ἄνδρας, ὧν ἁλῷ πόλις.
Wretched, just as men whose city is taken.
κακῶν δ᾽ ὥσπερ θάλασσα κῦμ᾽ ἄγει.
And like a sea of evils it brings a wave.
ὥσπερ τε πόλις καὶ τὸ δίκαιον ξυνεπαινεῖ.
Just as both the city and justice approve together.
εὐάγγελος μὲν, ὥσπερ ἡ παροιμία, ἕως γένοιτο.
A bearer of good news, as the proverb says, may he come.
τὸ μὴ πόλιν μὲν ὥσπερ οὖν ἔχει παθεῖν.
That the city not suffer as it is.
θαυμάζω δέ σου ἀλλόθρουν πόνον.
I marvel at your foreign toil.
ὥσπερ οὖν φονολιβεῖ τύχᾳ φρὴν ἐπιμαίνεται.
Just as in blood-dripping fortune the mind raves.
σῖγ᾽ ἀτίμως, ὥσπερ οὖν ἀπώλετο πατήρ.
In silence dishonored, just as his father perished.
λέγοις ἂν, ὥσπερ ἠδέσω τάφον πατρός.
You would speak, just as you honored your father's tomb.
ὥσπερ δεῦρ᾽ ἀπεζύγην πόδα.
Just as I yoked my foot here.
δόλοις ὀλούμεθ᾽, ὥσπερ οὖν ἐκτείναμεν.
We will perish by treachery, just as we killed.
ὥσπερ ξὺν ἵπποις.
Just as with horses.
ἀλιτών, ὥσπερ ὅδ᾽ ἁνήρ.
Having sinned, just as this man.
δρᾶσαι γὰρ, ὥσπερ ἔστιν, οὐκ ἀρνούμεθα.
For we do not deny that we did it, just as it is.
παῖδες θανόντες ὡσπερεὶ πρὸς τῶν φίλων.
Children dead as if by their friends.
οὐ προτιμῶν, ὡσπερεὶ βοτοῦ μόρον.
Not honoring, as if the fate of a beast.
τὸ μὴ φρονοῦν γὰρ, ὡσπερεὶ βοτὸν, τρέφειν ἀνάγκη.
For what has no mind, as if a beast, must be fed.

sense.def: (adverbium) sicut, velut, frequens apud epicos, lyricos et tragicos, alienum vero a prosa: de quo dictum est in Thes. vol. 8 p. 2127.
(adverb) as, like, frequent among epic, lyric, and tragic poets, but foreign to prose: on which see Thes. vol. 8 p. 2127.

cit.quote: κατώρυχες δ᾽ ἔναιον ὥστ᾽ ἀήσυροι μύρμηκες.
They dwelt in holes like airy ants.
ὥστε ναὸς κεδνός οἰακοστρόφος.
So that a trusted helmsman of the ship.
ὥστε θύννους ἤ τιν᾿ ἰχθύων βόλον.
Like tunas or some catch of fish.
ἔκυρσας, ὥστε τοξότης ἄκρος, σκοποῦ.
You hit, like a top archer, the mark.
λύκος γὰρ ὥστ᾽ ὠμόφρων.
For a wolf, like a savage-minded one.
ὥστ᾽ Αμαζόνος.
Like an Amazon.
ὥσθ᾽ ὑπογαίου βροντῆς.
Like underground thunder.
ὥστε παρθένοις ἁβραῖς.
Like delicate maidens.
ἀλέκτωρ ὥστε (sic Scaliger pro ὥσπερ).
A cock, as (thus Scaliger for ὥσπερ [just as]).
κόρακες ὥστε.
Like ravens.
ὥστε σύγγονον βροτοῖς (ἐστί).
So that it is akin to mortals.
ὥστε διπλόοι λύκοι νεβρόν φέρουσιν.
Like double wolves carrying a fawn.

sense.def: ὥστεso that, so as to ita ut, vel quamobrem, consequentiae significaudae serviens, sequente vel indicativo vel optativo cum ἄwhich (neuter plural relative pronoun) v, vel infinitivo. Aeschylus sola usus est structura cum infinitivo
ὥστε [so that] ita ut, or for which reason, serving to indicate consequence, followed by either indicative or optative with ἄν, or infinitive. Aeschylus used only the construction with infinitive

cit.quote: ὥστε σοι τὸν νῦν ὄχλον παρόντα μόχθων παιδιὰν εἶναι δοκεῖν.
So that the present crowd of toils seems to you a game.
αὐχῶ τήνδε δωρεὰν ἐμοὶ δώσειν Δί᾽, ὥστε τῶνδέ σ᾽ ἐκλῦσαι πόνων.
I boast that Zeus will give me this gift, so as to release you from these toils.
γνάψει γὰρ οὐδὲν τῶνδέ μ᾿ ὥστε καὶ φράσαι.
For he will not card me any of these things so as even to speak.
ἐμοιράσαντο δ᾽ ὀξυκάρδιοι κτήμαθ᾽, ὥστ᾽ ἴσον λαχεῖν.
They divided the possessions with sharp hearts, so as to get an equal share.
ὥστε Δαρείου πολύν τε καὶ καλὸν φθεῖραι στρατόν.
So as to destroy Darius's great and fine army.
πόσον τι πλῆθος ἦν νεῶν Ἑλληνίδων, ὥστ᾽ ἀξιῶσαι Περσικῷ στρατεύματι μάχην ξυνάψαι;
How great was the number of Greek ships, so as to deem it right to join battle with the Persian army?
ἀμφὶ δὲ κυκλοῦντο πᾶσαν νῆσον, ὥστ᾽ ἀμηχανεῖν ὅποι τράπεται.
They encircled the whole island, so that they were at a loss where to turn.
μηχαναῖς ἔζευξεν Ἕλλης πορθμόν, ὥστ᾽ ἔχειν πόρον.
He yoked the strait of Helle with devices, so as to have a passage.
καὶ τόδ᾽ ἐξέπραξεν, ὥστε Βόσπορον κλῆσαι μέγαν;
And did he accomplish this, so as to close the great Bosporus?
φεῦ μέγας τις ἦλθε δαίμων, ὥστε μὴ φρονεῖν καλῶς.
Alas, a great divinity came, so as not to think well.
ὥστε χθόνα βάκτροις ἐπικρούσαντας Ατρείδας δάκρυ μὴ κατασχεῖν.
So that the Atreidae, striking the ground with staffs, could not hold back tears.
πόντον ὥστε νωτίσαι.
So as to swim the sea.
ἔστω δ᾽ ἀπήμαντον, ὥστ᾽ ἀπαρκεῖν εὐ πραπίδων λαχόντα.
Let it be unharmed, so as to suffice for those who have obtained good fortune.
ὥστ᾽ ἐνδακρύειν γ᾽ ὄμμασιν χαρᾶς ὕπο.
So as to weep with eyes from joy.
οὐκ οἶδεν οὐδεὶς, ὥστ᾽ ἀπαγγείλαι τορῶς.
No one knows, so as to report clearly.
οὐ γὰρ τοιοῦτος, ὥστε θρηνητοῦ τυχεῖν.
For he is not such as to get a mourner.
ὥστε κύματος δίκην κλύζειν πρὸς αὐγὰς τοῦδε πήματος πολὺ μεῖζον.
So that like a wave it washes toward the light of this calamity much greater.
εἰ δ᾽ ἣν πρεπόντων ὥστ᾽ ἐπισπένδειν νεκρῷ.
But if it were fitting to pour libations to the dead.
ἢ καὶ πέπυσθε τοὔναρ, ὥστ᾽ ὀρθῶς φράσαι;
Or have you also heard the dream, so as to tell it correctly?
ὥστ᾽ ἐν γάλακτι θρόμβον αἵματος σπάσαι.
So as to draw a clot of blood in milk.
κρίνω δέ τοί νιν ὥστε συγκόλλως ἔχειν.
I judge him to be so as to hold together.
μενούμεν οὕτως, ὥστ᾽ ἐπεικάζειν τινά.
We will remain so, that someone may conjecture.
τί τῶνδ᾽ ἂν εἴποις ὥστε δηλῶσαι φρενί;
What of these things could you say so as to make clear to the mind?
οὐχ ὥστ᾽ (sic Porsonus pro ὡς δ᾽) ἀρῆξαι.
Not so as (thus Porson for ὡς δ᾽) to help.
ὥστ᾽ ἐς τὸ πᾶν σε τῶνδ᾽ ἀπαλλάξαι πόνων.
So as to release you entirely from these toils.
ἔχρησας ὥστε τὸν ξένον μητροκτονεῖν.
You prophesied so that the stranger should kill his mother.
οὐδ᾽ ἂν δεχοίμην ὥστ᾽ ἔχειν τιμὰς σέθεν.
Nor would I accept so as to have honors from you.
οὔτοι σ᾽ Ἀπόλλων ῥύσαιτ᾽ ἂν, ὥστε μὴ οὐ παρημελημένον ἔρρειν.
Apollo would not save you, so as not to go neglected.
σὺ τοῦτο πράξεις, ὥστε με σθένειν τόσον;
Will you do this, so that I have such strength?
ὥστ᾽ ἀνηβῆσαί με γηραιᾷ φρενί.
So as to make me young again in my aged mind.

sense.note: Cum indicativo
With indicative

cit.quote: ὥς (sic corrector: ὧδ᾽ pr. Μ) ἰδεῖν τέλος πάρεστιν οἷον ἤνυσεν κακόν.
Thus (the corrector: ὧδ᾽ first hand M) to see the end is present, what evil he accomplished.
πρὸς τάδ᾽ ὡς Σούσων μὲν ἄστυ πᾶν κενανδρίαν στένει.
In response to this, how the whole city of Susa laments the loss of men.
ὡς ἑκὼν ἐγὼ μαθοῦσιν αὐδῶ κοὐ μαθοῦσι λήθομαι.
As I willingly speak to those who understand, and to those who do not understand I am forgotten.
τὰ μηδὲν ὠφελοῦντα μὴ πόνει μάτην.
Do not toil in vain at things that help nothing.
μάτην γὰρ οὐδὲν ὠφελῶν ἐμοὶ πονήσεις.
For in vain you will toil, helping me nothing.
τοῖς θανοῦσι πλοῦτος οὐδὲν ὠφελεῖ.
Wealth helps the dead not at all.
μή νυν βροτοὺς μὲν ὠφέλει καιροῦ πέρα.
Do not help mortals beyond the proper time.

sense.def: Passivum ὠφελέομαι ίκνονI derive benefit , utilitatem capio.
Passive ὠφελέομαι ίκνον, I derive benefit

cit.quote: τοιάδ᾽ ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὁ τῶν θεῶν τύραννος ὠφελημένος.
Such things from me the tyrant of the gods has been helped.
μέγ᾽ ὠφέλημα τοῦτ᾽ ἐδωρήσω βροτοῖς.
You have given this great benefit to mortals.
ἔνερθε δὲ χθονός κεκρυμμέν᾽ ἀνθρώποισιν ὠφελήματα.
And beneath the earth are hidden benefits for humans.
ὦ κοινὸν ὠφέλημα θνητοῖσιν φανείς.
O common benefit appearing to mortals.
